/* Bootstrap table recording which migrations are already applied. It must
 * exist before the history can be read, so it cannot itself live in a
 * migration file - and its DDL differs per dialect (DATETIME vs TIMESTAMP).
 *
 * `query` is LONGTEXT on MySQL: the column holds whole migration files, and
 * TEXT stops at 64 KiB - a migration over that limit would be rejected
 * (strict mode) or truncated (non-strict), and a truncated history row can
 * never match the file again, which is a permanent mismatch on every open.
 * Databases created while this said TEXT are widened in create_schema_status()
 * with a best-effort ALTER right after the CREATE. */
static const char *const migrations_table_sql[SQL_LANG_COUNT] = {
    [SQL_SQLITE]   = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Migrations (\n"
                     "    applied_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n"
                     "    query TEXT NOT NULL\n"
                     ");\n",
    [SQL_MYSQL]    = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Migrations (\n"
                     "    applied_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n"
                     "    query LONGTEXT NOT NULL\n"
                     ");\n",
    [SQL_POSTGRES] = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Migrations (\n"
                     "    applied_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,\n"
                     "    query TEXT NOT NULL\n"
                     ");\n",
};

// Existing MySQL databases were created with `query TEXT`; widen them once.
// Idempotent (MODIFY to the same type succeeds), best-effort: a failure
// leaves the old limit in place and is logged by exec_script, never fatal.
static const char *const migrations_table_widen_sql[SQL_LANG_COUNT] = {
    [SQL_SQLITE]   = NULL,
    [SQL_MYSQL]    = "ALTER TABLE Migrations MODIFY query LONGTEXT NOT NULL;",
    [SQL_POSTGRES] = NULL,
};

/* Migration file contents for the active dialect, read from disk once per
 * process - the same lifetime the inline strings used to have.
 *
 * Indexed BY DIALECT, not by "the current dialect": a process may hold two
 * databases of different dialects open at the same time (webc_open_db_spec),
 * so one shared buffer that got reloaded whenever the dialect changed would
 * free text another connection is about to read. */
static String_Builder migration_bufs[SQL_LANG_COUNT][ARRAY_LEN(migrations)];
static bool migration_files_loaded[SQL_LANG_COUNT];

static bool migration_files_load(sql_lang_t lang) {
    if (lang >= SQL_LANG_COUNT) return false;
    if (migration_files_loaded[lang]) return true;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ARRAY_LEN(migrations); ++i) {
        const char *path = migrations[i].paths[lang];
        if (!path) {
            fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: migration %s has no file for SQL dialect %d\n",
                    migrations[i].name, (int) lang);
            return false;
        }
        if (!read_entire_file(path, &migration_bufs[lang][i])) return false;
        sb_append_null(&migration_bufs[lang][i]);  // callers treat items as a C string
    }
    migration_files_loaded[lang] = true;
    return true;
}

static const char *migration_sql(sql_lang_t lang, size_t index) {
    return migration_bufs[lang][index].items;
}

// Result of checking/applying the migrations history.
typedef enum {
    SCHEMA_OK = 0,            // history matches and all pending migrations are applied
    SCHEMA_ERROR,             // SQL/internal error (nothing was committed)
    SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH,  // an already-applied migration differs from the
                              // migration files (the history was rewritten)
                              // -> caller may rebuild
} Schema_Status;

static Schema_Status create_schema_status(db_t *db, const char *webc_path);

static Schema_Status create_schema_status(db_t *db, const char *webc_path) {
    Schema_Status result   = SCHEMA_OK;
    sql_stmt stmt          = {0};
    bool began             = false;
    bool fk_off            = false;
    char **stored          = NULL;      // history rows, copied out of the result
    size_t stored_count    = 0;
    size_t stored_capacity = 0;
    bool *stored_used      = NULL;      // which stored row matched a file
    bool *matched          = NULL;      // which migrations[] entry is applied

    if (!migration_files_load(db->lang)) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);

    // Migrations may swap a table other tables point at (0003 rebuilds the
    // demo `users` into the POS shape while notes.user_id references it).
    // SQLite enforces DROP/RENAME against live FKs and PRAGMA foreign_keys
    // is a no-op inside a transaction, so toggle it around the whole apply -
    // the same pattern the restore path below uses. Only the sqlite dialect
    // needs this: the ported mysql/postgres files carry no REFERENCES clauses
    // that could block a DROP.
    if (db->lang == SQL_SQLITE) {
        if (sqlite3_exec((sqlite3 *) db->conn, "PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF;",
                         NULL, NULL, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
            nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "disabling foreign keys for migrations: %s",
                    db_errmsg(db));
            return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
        }
        fk_off = true;
    }

    if (!sql_txn_begin(db)) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
    began = true;

    if (!sql_exec_script(db, migrations_table_sql[db->lang])) {
        return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
    }
    if (migrations_table_widen_sql[db->lang]) {
        // Best effort on purpose: databases created with the old `query TEXT`
        // keep working while it fails, and sql_exec_script() logs the reason.
        sql_exec_script(db, migrations_table_widen_sql[db->lang]);
    }

    if (!sql_prepare(db, "SELECT query FROM Migrations;", &stmt)) {
        return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
    }

    // Read the whole history before judging it. The table carries no ORDER BY
    // guarantee - InnoDB invents a hidden key when none is declared, Postgres
    // promises nothing - so rows are matched BY CONTENT below instead of by
    // position. Content matching keeps D5's property (an edited file can
    // never silently pass) without relying on an order no backend promises.
    Sql_Step rc = sql_step(&stmt);
    for (; rc == SQL_ROW; rc = sql_step(&stmt)) {
        if (stored_count >= stored_capacity) {
            size_t next = stored_capacity ? stored_capacity * 2 : 16;
            char **grown = realloc(stored, next * sizeof(*stored));
            if (!grown) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
            stored = grown;
            stored_capacity = next;
        }
        const char *query = sql_column_text(&stmt, 0);
        stored[stored_count] = strdup(query ? query : "");
        if (!stored[stored_count]) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
        stored_count += 1;
    }
    if (rc != SQL_DONE) {
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "reading migration history: %s", db_errmsg(db));
        return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
    }
    sql_finalize(&stmt);

    if (stored_count > ARRAY_LEN(migrations)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: %s: Database scheme is too new. Contains "
                "more migrations applied than expected. Update your "
                "application.\n", webc_path);
        return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
    }

    stored_used = calloc(stored_count ? stored_count : 1, sizeof(*stored_used));
    matched = calloc(ARRAY_LEN(migrations), sizeof(*matched));
    if (!stored_used || !matched) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);

    // Every stored row must be exactly some file's text, and every file
    // consumed at most one row. First-fit is enough: identical texts are
    // interchangeable, and a permutation of the real history still matches.
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ARRAY_LEN(migrations); ++i) {
        const char *expected = migration_sql(db->lang, i);
        if (!expected) continue;
        for (size_t j = 0; j < stored_count; ++j) {
            if (stored_used[j]) continue;
            if (strcmp(stored[j], expected) == 0) {
                stored_used[j] = true;
                matched[i] = true;
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // A row no migration file accounts for = history this checkout does not
    // own (the history was rewritten, or a shipped migration file was edited).
    // Same verdict as the old position-based compare: rebuild, or reject.
    for (size_t j = 0; j < stored_count; ++j) {
        if (stored_used[j]) continue;
        size_t i = 0;
        while (i < ARRAY_LEN(migrations) && matched[i]) ++i;
        const char *name     = i < ARRAY_LEN(migrations) ? migrations[i].name : "?";
        const char *expected = i < ARRAY_LEN(migrations)
                             ? migration_sql(db->lang, i) : "";
        fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: %s: Invalid database scheme. Mismatch in "
                "migration %s:\n", webc_path, name);
        fprintf(stderr, "EXPECTED: %s\n", expected);
        fprintf(stderr, "FOUND: %s\n", stored[j][0] ? stored[j] : "(null)");
        return_defer(SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH);
    }

    // Unmatched files are pending migrations (fewer rows than files is the
    // normal "some migrations not applied yet" state).
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ARRAY_LEN(migrations); ++i) {
        if (matched[i]) continue;
        printf("INFO: %s: applying migration %s\n", webc_path,
               migrations[i].name);
        const char *mig = migration_sql(db->lang, i);
        if (WEBC_TRACE_MIGRATION_QUERIES) printf("%s\n", mig);
        if (!sql_exec_script(db, mig)) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);

        if (!sql_prepare(db, "INSERT INTO Migrations (query) VALUES (?)",
                         &stmt)) {
            return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
        }
        bool ok = sql_bind(&stmt, 1, SQL_SV(sv_from_cstr(mig)))
                  && sql_final_step(&stmt);
        sql_finalize(&stmt);
        if (!ok) return_defer(SCHEMA_ERROR);
    }

defer:
    sql_finalize(&stmt);
    for (size_t j = 0; j < stored_count; ++j) free(stored[j]);
    free(stored);
    free(stored_used);
    free(matched);
    if (result == SCHEMA_OK) {
        if (!sql_txn_commit(db)) result = SCHEMA_ERROR;
    } else if (began) {
        // Nothing is committed on error/mismatch; close the open transaction
        // explicitly so the connection is in a clean state. (ROLLBACK outside
        // of a transaction just reports an error, which we skip.)
        sql_txn_rollback(db);
    }
    // Always restore FK enforcement for the request-serving connection,
    // whether the apply succeeded or bailed out half way.
    if (fk_off) {
        sqlite3_exec((sqlite3 *) db->conn, "PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;",
                     NULL, NULL, NULL);
    }
    return result;
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Backup/restore support: when migrations[] history was rewritten we rebuild
 * the database from scratch, but keep the user data:
 *   1. db            -> db.bak     (old file, untouched)
 *   2. fresh db is created and migrated from migrations[]
 *   3. every table/column both databases share is copied from db.bak into
 *      the new schema (db_restore_from_backup)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 */
static const char *db_backup_path(const char *path) {
    return temp_sprintf("%s.bak", path);
}

// Moves the current database file out of the way so a fresh one can be
// created. The connection MUST be closed before calling this (so SQLite has
// checkpointed and removed the -wal/-shm files). `path` is the sqlite file of
// the connection being rebuilt - not the process-wide global, so a database
// opened through webc_open_db_spec() rebuilds itself and not the primary one.
static bool db_backup_and_reset(const char *path) {
    const char *bak     = db_backup_path(path);
    const char *wal     = temp_sprintf("%s-wal", path);
    const char *shm     = temp_sprintf("%s-shm", path);
    const char *bak_wal = temp_sprintf("%s.bak-wal", path);
    const char *bak_shm = temp_sprintf("%s.bak-shm", path);

    if (file_exists(bak) > 0 && !delete_file(bak)) return false;
    if (file_exists(bak_wal) > 0 && !delete_file(bak_wal)) return false;
    if (file_exists(bak_shm) > 0 && !delete_file(bak_shm)) return false;

    if (!nob_rename(path, bak)) return false;

    // Leftovers of the renamed file must not be picked up by the new database
    if (file_exists(wal) > 0 && !delete_file(wal)) return false;
    if (file_exists(shm) > 0 && !delete_file(shm)) return false;
    return true;
}

static bool str_ieq(const char *a, const char *b) {
    size_t n = strlen(a);
    return n == strlen(b) && sqlite3_strnicmp(a, b, (int)n) == 0;
}

static void sb_append_quoted_ident(String_Builder *sb, const char *s) {
    sb_append_cstr(sb, "\"");
    for (; *s; ++s) {
        if (*s == '"') sb_append_cstr(sb, "\"\"");
        else sb_append_buf(sb, s, 1);
    }
    sb_append_cstr(sb, "\"");
}

#define MAX_TABLE_COLS 64
typedef struct {
    char name[128];
} Col_Name;
typedef struct {
    Col_Name items[MAX_TABLE_COLS];
    size_t count;
} Column_List;

// PRAGMA <schema>.table_info(<table>) -> column names of that table.
// A table that does not exist simply yields count == 0.
static bool get_table_columns(sqlite3     *db,
                              const char  *schema,
                              const char  *table,
                              Column_List *out)
{
    bool result = true;
    sqlite3_stmt *stmt = NULL;
    String_Builder sql = {0};

    out->count = 0;
    sb_append_cstr(&sql, "PRAGMA ");
    sb_append_cstr(&sql, schema);
    sb_append_cstr(&sql, ".table_info(");
    sb_append_quoted_ident(&sql, table);
    sb_append_cstr(&sql, ");");
    sb_append_null(&sql);

    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, sql.items, -1, &stmt, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
        LOG_SQLITE3_ERROR(db);
        return_defer(false);
    }

    while (sqlite3_step(stmt) == SQLITE_ROW) {
        const char *name = (const char *)sqlite3_column_text(stmt, 1);
        if (out->count >= MAX_TABLE_COLS) {
            fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: table `%s` has more than %d columns, "
                    "cannot restore it automatically\n", table, MAX_TABLE_COLS);
            return_defer(false);
        }
        snprintf(out->items[out->count].name, sizeof(out->items[0].name), "%s", name);
        out->count += 1;
    }

defer:
    if (stmt) sqlite3_finalize(stmt);
    sb_free(sql);
    return result;
}

// Copies all tables that exist in both databases (matching columns by name,
// case-insensitively) from the backup into the freshly migrated database.
// Foreign key checks are toggled off inside (the connection now comes up
// with them on) so rows can be inserted in any order.
static bool db_restore_from_backup(sqlite3 *db, const char *bak_path) {
    bool result = true;
    bool attached = false;
    sqlite3_stmt *tables_stmt = NULL;
    String_Builder sql = {0};
    char tables[64][128] = {0};
    size_t tables_count = 0;

    sb_append_cstr(&sql, "ATTACH DATABASE '");
    for (const char *p = bak_path; *p; ++p) {
        if (*p == '\'') sb_append_cstr(&sql, "''");
        else sb_append_buf(&sql, p, 1);
    }
    sb_append_cstr(&sql, "' AS bak");
    sb_append_null(&sql);

    if (sqlite3_exec(db, sql.items, NULL, NULL, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
        LOG_SQLITE3_ERROR(db);
        return_defer(false);
    }
    attached = true;

    // Run the copy with foreign key checks off: a note may reference a user
    // that is restored later. Re-enabled in the defer below, which always
    // runs outside the transaction.
    if (sqlite3_exec(db, "PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF;", NULL, NULL, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
        LOG_SQLITE3_ERROR(db);
        return_defer(false);
    }

    if (!txn_begin(db)) return_defer(false);

    // Materialize the table list first so we do not hold a statement open
    // while inserting into the main database.
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db,
            "SELECT name FROM bak.sqlite_master WHERE type='table' "
            "AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' AND name <> 'Migrations' ORDER BY name;",
            -1, &tables_stmt, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
        LOG_SQLITE3_ERROR(db);
        return_defer(false);
    }

    int step = SQLITE_ROW;
    while ((step = sqlite3_step(tables_stmt)) == SQLITE_ROW) {
        const char *name = (const char *)sqlite3_column_text(tables_stmt, 0);
        if (tables_count >= ARRAY_LEN(tables)) {
            fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: backup contains more than %zu tables, "
                    "cannot restore it automatically\n", ARRAY_LEN(tables));
            return_defer(false);
        }
        snprintf(tables[tables_count], sizeof(tables[0]), "%s", name);
        tables_count += 1;
    }
    if (step != SQLITE_DONE) {
        LOG_SQLITE3_ERROR(db);
        return_defer(false);
    }
    sqlite3_finalize(tables_stmt);
    tables_stmt = NULL;

    for (size_t i = 0; i < tables_count; ++i) {
        const char *old_name = tables[i];
        Column_List old_cols = {0}, new_cols = {0};

        if (!get_table_columns(db, "bak", old_name, &old_cols)) return_defer(false);
        if (!get_table_columns(db, "main", old_name, &new_cols)) return_defer(false);

        if (new_cols.count == 0) {
            printf("INFO: backup table `%s` has no counterpart in the new "
                    "schema, skipped\n", old_name);
            continue;
        }

        String_Builder cols = {0};
        String_Builder sel = {0};
        size_t shared = 0;
        for (size_t j = 0; j < new_cols.count; ++j) {
            const char *col = new_cols.items[j].name;
            bool exists = false;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < old_cols.count; ++k) {
                if (str_ieq(col, old_cols.items[k].name)) {
                    exists = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!exists) continue;
            if (shared > 0) {
                sb_append_cstr(&cols, ", ");
                sb_append_cstr(&sel, ", ");
            }
            sb_append_quoted_ident(&cols, col);
            sb_append_quoted_ident(&sel, col);
            shared += 1;
        }

        if (shared == 0) {
            printf("INFO: backup table `%s` shares no columns with the new "
                    "schema, skipped\n", old_name);
            sb_free(cols);
            sb_free(sel);
            continue;
        }

        sql.count = 0;
        sb_append_cstr(&sql, "INSERT INTO ");
        sb_append_quoted_ident(&sql, old_name);
        sb_append_cstr(&sql, " (");
        sb_append_buf(&sql, cols.items, cols.count);
        sb_append_cstr(&sql, ") SELECT ");
        sb_append_buf(&sql, sel.items, sel.count);
        sb_append_cstr(&sql, " FROM bak.");
        sb_append_quoted_ident(&sql, old_name);
        sb_append_cstr(&sql, ";");
        sb_append_null(&sql);
        sb_free(cols);
        sb_free(sel);

        if (sqlite3_exec(db, sql.items, NULL, NULL, NULL) != SQLITE_OK) {
            fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: restoring table `%s` failed: %s\n",
                    old_name, sqlite3_errmsg(db));
            return_defer(false);
        }
        printf("INFO: restored %d row(s) into `%s`\n", sqlite3_changes(db), old_name);
    }

    if (!txn_commit(db)) return_defer(false);

defer:
    if (tables_stmt) sqlite3_finalize(tables_stmt);
    if (!result) sqlite3_exec(db, "ROLLBACK;", NULL, NULL, NULL);
    if (attached) sqlite3_exec(db, "DETACH DATABASE bak;", NULL, NULL, NULL);
    sqlite3_exec(db, "PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;", NULL, NULL, NULL);
    sb_free(sql);
    return result;
}

/* -- dialect + connection string ------------------------------------------
 * Resolution order:
 *   1. WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL - "SQLITE3"/"MYSQL"/"POSTGRES" (case-insensitive),
 *      the explicit choice; the prefix is then only used to find the DSN.
 *   2. `mysql:` / `postgres:` prefix on WEBC_DB_PATH - one variable that
 *      carries both dialect and connection string.
 *   3. SQLite - the default, and also the answer when WEBC_DB_PATH is still
 *      NULL (this is reachable: the globals are read by code that can run
 *      before main() has set them, and a NULL must not segfault).
 */
sql_lang_t webc_db_lang(void) {
    if (WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL && WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL[0]) {
        if (str_ieq(WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL, "SQLITE") ||
            str_ieq(WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL, "SQLITE3")) return SQL_SQLITE;
        if (str_ieq(WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL, "MYSQL")) return SQL_MYSQL;
        if (str_ieq(WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL, "POSTGRES") ||
            str_ieq(WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL, "POSTGRESQL")) return SQL_POSTGRES;
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL: unknown dialect `%s` "
                "(want SQLITE3, MYSQL or POSTGRES); falling back to the "
                "WEBC_DB prefix", WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL);
    }
    if (!WEBC_DB_PATH) return SQL_SQLITE;
    if (strncmp(WEBC_DB_PATH, "mysql:", 6) == 0) return SQL_MYSQL;
    if (strncmp(WEBC_DB_PATH, "postgres:", 9) == 0) return SQL_POSTGRES;
    return SQL_SQLITE;
}

const char *webc_db_dsn(void) {
    if (!WEBC_DB_PATH) return "";  // db_open() rejects an empty dsn
    sql_lang_t lang = webc_db_lang();
    if (lang == SQL_MYSQL && strncmp(WEBC_DB_PATH, "mysql:", 6) == 0) {
        return WEBC_DB_PATH + 6;
    }
    if (lang == SQL_POSTGRES && strncmp(WEBC_DB_PATH, "postgres:", 9) == 0) {
        return WEBC_DB_PATH + 9;
    }
    return WEBC_DB_PATH;
}

/* -- schema verification cache --------------------------------------------
 * create_schema_status() reads the whole migration history (2.4 MB of
 * 0009_geo_admin) and runs DDL. Its verdict depends only on (dialect, dsn),
 * so it is computed once per pair per process; every later open of the same
 * database just gets a fresh connection. Without this the pool would check
 * the same history 8 times at startup, and the old per-request open checked
 * it on EVERY request. A database modified by another process mid-run is not
 * re-detected - the same trade-off every migration tool makes. */
typedef struct {
    sql_lang_t lang;
    char      *dsn;
} Verified_Db;
static Verified_Db *verified_items = NULL;
static size_t verified_count = 0;

static bool schema_verified_has(sql_lang_t lang, const char *dsn) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < verified_count; ++i) {
        if (verified_items[i].lang == lang &&
            strcmp(verified_items[i].dsn, dsn) == 0) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

static void schema_verified_add(sql_lang_t lang, const char *dsn) {
    // A cache: losing an entry only costs a repeat of the check, so an
    // allocation failure is silently tolerated.
    Verified_Db *grown = realloc(verified_items,
                                 (verified_count + 1) * sizeof(*verified_items));
    if (!grown) return;
    verified_items = grown;
    char *copy = strdup(dsn);
    if (!copy) return;
    verified_items[verified_count].lang = lang;
    verified_items[verified_count].dsn = copy;
    verified_count += 1;
}

// Opens one connection and proves its schema (once per process per pair).
// `label` is what messages name (the spec the caller asked for); `dsn` is
// what the driver gets and, for sqlite, what the rebuild path renames.
// `symlink_hint` explains a failed sqlite open when WEBC_DIR_PATH is a
// symlink (primary-database legacy behaviour).
static void print_symlink_note(void);
static db_t *db_open_checked(sql_lang_t lang, const char *dsn,
                             const char *label, bool symlink_hint)
{
    bool open_failed = false;

    if (schema_verified_has(lang, dsn)) {
        db_t *db = db_open(lang, dsn);
        if (!db) open_failed = true;
        if (open_failed && symlink_hint) print_symlink_note();
        return open_failed ? NULL : db;
    }

    bool rebuilt = false;
    for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 2; ++attempt) {
        // db_open creates parent directories and applies the connection
        // PRAGMAs (WAL, synchronous, foreign_keys, cache/temp/mmap) -
        // everything SQLite refuses to run inside a transaction, so it all
        // happens before create_schema_status() opens one.
        db_t *db = db_open(lang, dsn);
        if (!db) {
            if (symlink_hint) print_symlink_note();
            return NULL;
        }

        Schema_Status status = create_schema_status(db, label);
        if (status == SCHEMA_OK) {
            schema_verified_add(lang, dsn);
            if (rebuilt) {
                const char *bak = db_backup_path(dsn);
                if (!db_restore_from_backup((sqlite3 *) db->conn, bak)) {
                    fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: could not copy the data back from "
                            "%s. Your previous data is still safe there; the "
                            "application continues with an empty schema.\n", bak);
                }
            }
            return db;
        }

        if (status == SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH && attempt == 0
            && lang == SQL_SQLITE) {
            // migrations[] history was rewritten: move the old database aside,
            // rebuild from scratch and copy the data over afterwards.
            fprintf(stderr, "NOTE: migrations[] history changed. Backing up "
                    "%s to %s and rebuilding the schema...\n",
                    label, db_backup_path(dsn));
            db_close(db);
            if (!db_backup_and_reset(dsn)) return NULL;
            rebuilt = true;
            continue;
        }

        if (status == SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH) {
            fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: %s: migration history does not match the "
                    "migration files; the automatic rebuild exists only for "
                    "the sqlite dialect - fix or recreate the database.\n",
                    label);
        }
        db_close(db);
        return NULL;
    }
    return NULL;  // attempt 1 either returned above or failed open/verify
}

// Legacy file->directory layout dance for the PRIMARY sqlite database (extra
// databases come from webc_open_db_spec(); the sqlite driver creates their
// parent directories itself). Sets *symlink_hint when WEBC_DIR_PATH is a
// symlink, so a later failed open can explain it.
static bool webc_prepare_primary_layout(bool *symlink_hint) {
    int exists = file_exists(WEBC_DIR_PATH);
    if (exists < 0) return false;

    if (!exists) {
        if (!db_mkdir_recursive(WEBC_DIR_PATH)) return false;
        return true;
    }

    File_Type type = get_file_type(WEBC_DIR_PATH);
    if (type < 0) return false;
    switch (type) {
    case FILE_DIRECTORY: break;
    case FILE_REGULAR: {
        nob_log(INFO, "%s is a file! Migrating it to a directory...", WEBC_DIR_PATH);
        const char *webc_tmp_db_path = temp_sprintf("%s.tmp", WEBC_DIR_PATH);
        if (!nob_rename(WEBC_DIR_PATH, webc_tmp_db_path)) return false;
        if (!db_mkdir_recursive(WEBC_DIR_PATH)) return false;
        if (!nob_rename(webc_tmp_db_path, WEBC_DB_PATH)) return false;
    } break;
    case FILE_SYMLINK: {
        *symlink_hint = true;
    } break;
    case FILE_OTHER: {
        fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: %s is a weird file! We expect it to be a "
                "directory or a regular file in case of a legacy database...\n",
                WEBC_DIR_PATH);
        return false;
    } break;
    }
    return true;
}

static void print_symlink_note(void) {
    if (!WEBC_DIR_PATH || !WEBC_DB_PATH) return;
    fprintf(stderr, "NOTE: Your %s is a symlink! We used to expect this "
            "path to lead to an sqlite3 database file, but at some point "
            "we changed it to a directory. And now the database file is "
            "expected to be at %s. If you are using some clever symlink "
            "setup, please update it accordingly so we could open %s as "
            "the sqlite3 database.\n", WEBC_DIR_PATH, WEBC_DB_PATH, WEBC_DB_PATH);
}

// Primary database, opened directly (this is what the pool is filled with).
static db_t *open_webc_db_raw(void) {
    if (!WEBC_DB_PATH || !WEBC_DB_PATH[0]) {
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "no database configured - set WEBC_DB or "
                "WEBC_CONNECTION_STRING, or edit WEBC_DEFAULT_DSN in "
                "src/webc.c");
        return NULL;
    }
    sql_lang_t lang = webc_db_lang();
    const char *dsn = webc_db_dsn();
    bool symlink_hint = false;

    if (lang == SQL_SQLITE && !webc_prepare_primary_layout(&symlink_hint)) {
        return NULL;
    }
    return db_open_checked(lang, dsn, WEBC_DB_PATH, symlink_hint);
}

db_t *webc_open_db_spec(const char *spec) {
    if (!spec || !spec[0]) return NULL;

    sql_lang_t lang;
    const char *dsn;
    if (strncmp(spec, "mysql:", 6) == 0) {
        lang = SQL_MYSQL;
        dsn = spec + 6;
    } else if (strncmp(spec, "postgres:", 9) == 0) {
        lang = SQL_POSTGRES;
        dsn = spec + 9;
    } else {
        // No prefix on the spec: an explicit WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL decides,
        // otherwise a bare path/DSN means SQLite (the WEBC_DB prefix is a
        // property of the PRIMARY database and must not leak in here).
        lang = SQL_SQLITE;
        if (WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL && WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL[0]) lang = webc_db_lang();
        dsn = spec;
    }

    db_t *db = db_open_checked(lang, dsn, spec, false);
    if (db) db->pool_slot = -1;  // caller owns it; db_close() destroys it
    return db;
}

/* -- connection pool (primary database) -----------------------------------
 * LAZY + grow-on-demand: nothing connects at startup (serve.c does not
 * warm the pool - a static file server or `webc help` never touches a
 * database). The first checkout opens connection 1; later checkouts open
 * another slot only when every existing one is genuinely in use, up to
 * DB_POOL_SIZE. Every slot tracks in_use, so a caller never holds two
 * handles, and db_close() releases it (pooled handles carry pool_slot >= 0,
 * so every existing `open_webc_db(); ...; db_close();` call site keeps
 * working unchanged).
 *
 * Release undoes what a request left behind before the next one sees it:
 *   - an open transaction is rolled back (a handler that returned between
 *     BEGIN and COMMIT must not leak its txn onto a shared handle);
 *   - a sqlite connection with a leaked statement is recycled, because a
 *     leaked statement pins a read transaction on a handle others share.
 *
 * The FIRST open failure LATCHES the pool: db_pool_get() returns NULL
 * forever after (one error, no per-request retry storm). A failed GROW
 * later on does not latch - it degrades to a transient, unpooled
 * connection so a burst costs "one connection per request" instead of a
 * 500. One process talks to exactly one server: every slot opens the same
 * primary DSN. */
typedef struct {
    db_t *db;
    bool  in_use;
} Pool_Slot;

static Pool_Slot db_pool[DB_POOL_SIZE];
static int db_pool_index = 0;
static int  db_pool_count = 0;        // slots open so far (lazy: 0 at start)
static bool db_pool_latched = false;  // first open failed -> refuse forever

// The "not pooled" teardown: close the connection and free the handle.
static void db_destroy(db_t *db) {
    if (!db) return;
    if (db->drv && db->drv->close) db->drv->close(db);
    free(db->dsn);
    free(db);
}

// Open one more slot at the next index. False = open failed; the caller
// decides what that means (first ever open -> latch, later grow -> degrade
// to a transient connection).
static bool pool_grow(void) {
    db_t *db = open_webc_db_raw();
    if (!db) {
        fprintf(stderr, "ERROR: Failed to initialize DB pool connection %d\n",
                db_pool_count);
        return false;
    }
    db->pool_slot = db_pool_count;
    db_pool[db_pool_count].db = db;
    db_pool[db_pool_count].in_use = false;
    db_pool_count++;
    if (db_pool_count == 1)
        nob_log(NOB_INFO, "DB pool: first connection open (lazy)");
    return true;
}

// Hand a pooled connection back. Idempotent: releasing a slot that is already
// free (double close) is ignored rather than double-freed.
static void db_pool_release(db_t *db) {
    if (!db || db->pool_slot < 0) return;
    int slot = db->pool_slot;
    if (slot >= DB_POOL_SIZE || db_pool[slot].db != db
        || !db_pool[slot].in_use) {
        return;
    }

    if (db->txn_depth > 0) {
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "db_close: %s returned with %d open transaction(s); "
                "rolling back", db->dsn ? db->dsn : "connection", db->txn_depth);
        if (db->drv && db->drv->txn_rollback) db->drv->txn_rollback(db);
        db->txn_depth = 0;
    }

    if (db->lang == SQL_SQLITE && db->conn
        && sqlite3_next_stmt((sqlite3 *) db->conn, NULL)) {
        // Recycle: sqlite3_close() below becomes close_v2() (a zombie kept
        // alive by the leaked statement), and the slot gets a clean handle
        // with all connection PRAGMAs applied again.
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "db_close: leaked statement on %s; recycling the "
                "pooled connection", db->dsn ? db->dsn : "connection");
        db->drv->close(db);
        db->conn = NULL;
        if (db->drv->open(db, db->dsn)) {
            db->txn_depth = 0;
        } else {
            nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "db_close: could not recycle %s (%s); dropping "
                    "the pool slot", db->dsn ? db->dsn : "connection",
                    db->err[0] ? db->err : db->drv->errmsg(db));
            db_destroy(db);
            db_pool[slot] = (Pool_Slot) {0};
            return;
        }
    }

    db_pool[slot].in_use = false;
}

db_t *db_pool_get(void) {
    if (db_pool_latched) return NULL;  // one clean refusal, no storm

    // First use opens connection 1; its failure latches the pool (bad DSN
    // or refused schema: fail once, then every request gets NULL).
    if (db_pool_count == 0 && !pool_grow()) {
        db_pool_latched = true;
        return NULL;
    }

    for (int n = 0; n < db_pool_count; ++n) {
        int i = (db_pool_index + n) % db_pool_count;
        if (!db_pool[i].db || db_pool[i].in_use) continue;
        db_pool[i].in_use = true;
        db_pool_index = (i + 1) % db_pool_count;
        return db_pool[i].db;
    }

    // Every slot busy: grow toward DB_POOL_SIZE. A failed grow does not
    // latch (the pool itself is serving) - fall through to transient.
    if (db_pool_count < DB_POOL_SIZE && pool_grow()) {
        int i = db_pool_count - 1;
        db_pool[i].in_use = true;
        db_pool_index = (i + 1) % db_pool_count;
        return db_pool[i].db;
    }

    // Degraded: a transient connection (pool_slot -1, destroyed by
    // db_close) so a burst costs one connection per request instead of a 500.
    db_t *db = open_webc_db_raw();
    if (db) db->pool_slot = -1;
    return db;
}

db_t *open_webc_db(void) {
    // Pool checkout: call sites keep their `open_webc_db(); ...; db_close();`
    // shape, the pool and the once-per-database schema check are invisible
    // to them. NULL means "the database is unavailable" (serve 500), which
    // every call site already handles.
    return db_pool_get();
}

void db_close(db_t *db) {
    if (!db) return;
    if (db->pool_slot >= 0) {
        db_pool_release(db);
        return;
    }
    db_destroy(db);
}

#ifndef MASTER_CHILD_H_
#define MASTER_CHILD_H_

#include "../http/serve.h"

// =========================================================================
// Master-child view interface.
//
// Stable API: modules compose their own MD_MasterConfig (column shapes come
// from the entity files) and hand it to serve_master_child(). Adding another
// master-child page never requires editing this header or its engine.
// =========================================================================

typedef struct {
    const char *id;     /* TEXT pk (legacy numeric string or uuid) */
    char       *label;
} MD_Option;

typedef enum {
    COL_TYPE_TEXT,
    COL_TYPE_NUM,
    COL_TYPE_DATE,
    COL_TYPE_TEXTAREA,
    COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT,
    COL_TYPE_IMG,
    COL_TYPE_COMPOSITE,
} Col_Type;

typedef struct MD_Column {
    const char       *name;
    const char       *label;
    Col_Type          type;
    int               nullable;
    const char       *fk_table;
    const char       *fk_label;
    const char       *fk_where;   /* raw WHERE fragment scoping the option query */
    const char       *fk_value;
    MD_Option        *opt;        /* runtime: FK dropdown options */
    size_t            opt_count;
    int               fk_cascade; /* leaf of a parent-scoped cascade */
    int               hidden;     /* never displayed; preserved via hidden input
                                     on edit */
    int               computed;   /* display-only value (server-derived);
                                     no form input */

    /* Sub-columns for composite cells */
    const char       *style;        /* "stack", "avatar", "activity" */
    struct MD_Column *subcols;      /* Array of child sub-columns */
    size_t            subcol_count; /* Number of sub-columns */
    const char       *read_sql;     /* Custom read/CASE SQL expression */
    const char      **choices;      /* NULL-terminated choice string list */
} MD_Column;

#define MD_FIELD(name_, label_, type_, ...) \
    ((MD_Column) { .name = (name_), .label = (label_), .type = (type_), __VA_ARGS__ })

#define MD_FK(name_, label_, table_, where_, ...) \
    ((MD_Column){ .name = (name_), .label = (label_), .type = COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT, .fk_table = (table_), .fk_label = "label", .fk_where = (where_), __VA_ARGS__ })

#define MD_CHOICE(name_, label_, choices_, ...) \
    ((MD_Column){ .name = (name_), .label = (label_), .type = COL_TYPE_TEXT, .choices = (choices_), __VA_ARGS__ })

#define MD_STACK(label_, ...) \
    { .label = (label_), .type = COL_TYPE_COMPOSITE, .style = "stack", \
      .subcols = (MD_Column[]){ __VA_ARGS__ }, \
      .subcol_count = sizeof((MD_Column[]){ __VA_ARGS__ }) / sizeof(MD_Column) }

#define MD_AVATAR(label_, ...) \
    { .label = (label_), .type = COL_TYPE_COMPOSITE, .style = "avatar", \
      .subcols = (MD_Column[]){ __VA_ARGS__ }, \
      .subcol_count = sizeof((MD_Column[]){ __VA_ARGS__ }) / sizeof(MD_Column) }

#define MD_ACTIVITY(label_, ...) \
    { .label = (label_), .type = COL_TYPE_COMPOSITE, .style = "activity", .computed = 1, \
      .subcols = (MD_Column[]){ __VA_ARGS__ }, \
      .subcol_count = sizeof((MD_Column[]){ __VA_ARGS__ }) / sizeof(MD_Column) }

/* values[0] is the row id; column ci starts at its first slot below. Flat
 * columns keep the historic values[ci + 1] identity; a composite column
 * spans subcol_count slots. */
static inline size_t md_col_slot(const MD_Column *cols, size_t ci) {
    size_t slot = 1;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < ci; ++i) {
        if (cols[i].subcols != NULL && cols[i].subcol_count > 0) {
            slot += cols[i].subcol_count;
        } else {
            slot += 1;
        }
    }
    return slot;
}

/* Is this FK id among the column's offered (LIVE-only) options? */
static inline int md_opt_has_id(const MD_Column *col, const char *id) {
    if (col == NULL || id == NULL || id[0] == '\0') {
        return 0;
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < col->opt_count; ++i) {
        if (strcmp(id, col->opt[i].id) == 0) {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

typedef struct {
    char  **values;
    char  **disp;
    size_t  value_count;
} MD_ChildRow;

typedef struct {
    MD_ChildRow *items;
    size_t       count;
    size_t       capacity;
} MD_ChildRows;

typedef struct {
    const char  *table;
    const char  *title;
    const char  *fk_column;
    const char  *fk_subquery;
    const char  *id_column;
    const char  *crud_path;
    MD_Column   *columns;
    size_t       column_count;
    const char **sum_columns;
    size_t       sum_column_count;
    int          soft_delete;
} MD_ChildTab;

typedef struct {
    const char   *table;
    const char   *title;
    const char   *id_column;
    const char   *crud_path;   /* POST base: /create, /{id}/update|delete */
    MD_Column    *columns;
    size_t        column_count;
    const char  **sum_columns;
    size_t        sum_column_count;
    MD_ChildTab  *children;
    size_t        children_count;
    int           soft_delete;
    int           read_only;
    int           no_live;
    int           no_create;
    int           create_only;
} MD_MasterConfig;

typedef struct {
    MD_Column *col;
    MD_Option *items;
    size_t     count;
    size_t     capacity;
} MD_FormCol;

typedef struct {
    MD_FormCol *items;
    size_t      count;
    size_t      capacity;
} MD_FormCols;

typedef struct {
    const char    *id;
    char         **values;
    char         **disp;
    size_t         value_count;
    MD_ChildRows  *children;
    size_t         children_count;
} MD_MasterRow;

typedef struct {
    MD_MasterRow *items;
    size_t        count;
    size_t        capacity;
} MD_MasterRows;

const char *md_cascade_json(db_t *db, const MD_MasterRows *rows,
                            const MD_MasterConfig *config);

void serve_master_child(Serve_Context *sc, const MD_MasterConfig *config);

#endif // MASTER_CHILD_H_

#include "third_party/nob/nob.h"
#include "../auth/auth.h"
#include "../i18n/i18n.h"

// Sidebar identity HTML: the signed-in user's picture (ringed by account
// status) or an initials circle; nobody signed in -> generic workspace
// avatar. Temp-arena owned.
static const char *sidebar_avatar_html(const Auth_User *au) {
    const char *ring = "";
    if (au && au->status && au->status[0]) {
        if (strcmp(au->status, "ACTIVE") == 0)         ring = " ring-2 ring-blue";
        else if (strcmp(au->status, "INACTIVE") == 0)  ring = " ring-2 ring-peach";
        else if (strcmp(au->status, "SUSPENDED") == 0) ring = " ring-2 ring-red";
    }
    if (au && au->profile_pic && au->profile_pic[0]) {
        String_Builder sb = {0};
        sb_append_cstr(&sb, "<img src=\"");
        sb_append_html_escaped(&sb, au->profile_pic);
        sb_append_cstr(&sb, temp_sprintf(
            "\" alt=\"\" class=\"h-10 w-10 rounded-full object-cover shrink-0%s\">",
            ring));
        sb_append_null(&sb);
        return temp_strdup(sb.items);
    }
    const char *name = (au && au->name && au->name[0]) ? au->name : "";
    char initial[8] = {0};
    if (name[0]) {
        const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *) name;
        size_t n = 1;
        if ((p[0] & 0xE0) == 0xC0)      n = 2;
        else if ((p[0] & 0xF0) == 0xE0) n = 3;
        else if ((p[0] & 0xF8) == 0xF0) n = 4;
        memcpy(initial, name, n < sizeof(initial) ? n : sizeof(initial) - 1);
    }
    return temp_sprintf(
        "<span class=\"h-10 w-10 rounded-full shrink-0 inline-flex"
        " items-center justify-center text-sm font-semibold"
        " bg-surface1 text-subtext0%s\">%s</span>",
        ring, initial[0] ? initial : "?");
}

void render_page_header(String_Builder *sb,
                        const char     *page_title,
                        const char     *current_path)
{
    const Auth_User *au = auth_current_user();
    // Sidebar card: name + role (fallback email, then the workspace label).
    const char *u_name = (au && au->name && au->name[0]) ? au->name : "";
    const char *u_sub;
    if (au && au->role && au->role[0])       u_sub = au->role;
    else if (au && au->email && au->email[0]) u_sub = au->email;
    else                                      u_sub = "Staff workspace";
    const char *u_avatar = sidebar_avatar_html(au);
#define OUT(buf, size) sb_append_buf(sb, buf, size);
#define STR(x) sb_append_cstr(sb, (x) ? (x) : "");
#define CLS(cond, t, f) sb_append_cstr(sb, (cond) ? (t) : (f));
#define NAV_ACTIVE(prefix) (strncmp((current_path), (prefix), strlen(prefix)) == 0)
#define CURRENT_PATH current_path
#define PAGE_TITLE page_title
// Phase 12: <html lang> follows the active language, the top bar carries
// the language <select> (back = the page being rendered).
#define HTML_LANG i18n_html_lang()
#define LANG_FORM i18n_lang_form_html(current_path)
// Phase 13: sidebar card renders the signed-in session user (auth.c), not
// the first row of the users table.
#define SIDEBAR_AVATAR_RAW u_avatar
#define SIDEBAR_NAME u_name
#define SIDEBAR_SUB u_sub
#include "../../build/h_to_html/layout/header.h"
#undef SIDEBAR_SUB
#undef SIDEBAR_NAME
#undef SIDEBAR_AVATAR_RAW
#undef LANG_FORM
#undef HTML_LANG
#undef PAGE_TITLE
#undef CURRENT_PATH
#undef NAV_ACTIVE
#undef CLS
#undef STR
#undef OUT
}

FILE: src/layout/master_child.c

#define NOB_STRIP_PREFIX
#include "third_party/nob/nob.h"

#include "master_child.h"
#include "src/db/db.h"
#include "src/helper/cells.h"
#include "src/layout/header.h"
#include "src/layout/footer.h"
#include "src/http/utils.h"
#include "src/layout/paging.h"

// =========================================================================
// Master-child view engine: loads a configured master table plus its child
// tabs and renders the page. Pure interface implementation -- no knowledge
// of any concrete page (see people.c for the /people composition).
// =========================================================================

// ---- data loading -------------------------------------------------------

static MD_MasterRows *md_master_rows_new(void) {
    MD_MasterRows *rows = malloc(sizeof(MD_MasterRows));
    rows->items = NULL;
    rows->count = 0;
    rows->capacity = 0;
    return rows;
}

static void md_master_rows_free(MD_MasterRows *rows) {
    if (!rows) return;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < rows->count; ++i) {
        MD_MasterRow *row = &rows->items[i];
        free(row->values);
        free(row->disp);
        if (row->children) {
            for (size_t ci = 0; ci < row->children_count; ++ci) {
                MD_ChildRows *crows = &row->children[ci];
                free(crows->items);
            }
            free(row->children);
        }
    }
    free(rows->items);
    free(rows);
}

static char *col_to_str(sql_stmt *stmt, int col) {
    const char *val = sql_column_text(stmt, col);
    return val ? temp_strdup(val) : temp_strdup("");
}

// Quote a TEXT id for literal use in generated SQL (' -> '').
static const char *md_sql_quote(const char *s) {
    String_Builder sb = {0};
    for (const char *p = s; *p; ++p) {
        if (*p == '\'') sb_append_cstr(&sb, "''");
        else sb_append_buf(&sb, p, 1);
    }
    sb_append_null(&sb);
    char *copy = temp_strdup(sb.items);
    sb_free(sb);
    return copy;
}

static const char *md_col_sql(const MD_Column *col) {
    if (col->read_sql != NULL && col->read_sql[0] != '\0') {
        return col->read_sql;
    }
    return col->name;
}

static char *build_column_list(const MD_ChildTab *child) {
    String_Builder sb = {0};
    sb_append_cstr(&sb, child->id_column);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < child->column_count; ++i) {
        const MD_Column *col = &child->columns[i];
        if (col->subcols != NULL && col->subcol_count > 0) {
            for (size_t p = 0; p < col->subcol_count; ++p) {
                sb_append_cstr(&sb, ", ");
                sb_append_cstr(&sb, md_col_sql(&col->subcols[p]));
            }
        } else {
            sb_append_cstr(&sb, ", ");
            sb_append_cstr(&sb, md_col_sql(col));
        }
    }
    sb_append_null(&sb);
    return sb.items;
}

static bool load_child_rows(db_t              *db,
                            const MD_ChildTab *child,
                            const char        *master_id,
                            bool               show_deleted,
                            MD_ChildRows      *out_rows)
{
    char *cols = build_column_list(child);
    char *where_fk = NULL;
    // Same live/trash rule as the master list: soft_delete tabs hide the
    // trash, ?deleted=1 shows ONLY the trash (restore buttons gate on it).
    const char *trash = "";
    if (child->soft_delete) {
        trash = show_deleted ? " AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL"
                             : " AND deleted_at IS NULL";
    }
    if (child->fk_subquery != NULL) {
        where_fk = temp_sprintf(child->fk_subquery, md_sql_quote(master_id));
    } else {
        where_fk = temp_sprintf("%s = '%s'", child->fk_column,
                                md_sql_quote(master_id));
    }
    char *sql = temp_sprintf("SELECT %s FROM %s WHERE %s%s "
                             "ORDER BY %s DESC;",
                             cols, child->table, where_fk, trash,
                             child->id_column);
    sql_stmt stmt = {0};
    if (!sql_prepare(db, sql, &stmt)) {
        return false;
    }
    Sql_Step ret;
    for (ret = sql_step(&stmt); ret == SQL_ROW; ret = sql_step(&stmt)) {
        int col_count = sql_column_count(&stmt);
        MD_ChildRow row = {0};
        row.value_count = col_count;
        row.values = malloc(col_count * sizeof(char *));
        row.disp   = malloc(col_count * sizeof(char *));
        for (int i = 0; i < col_count; ++i) {
            row.values[i] = col_to_str(&stmt, i);
            row.disp[i]   = temp_strdup(row.values[i]);
        }
        da_append(out_rows, row);
    }
    if (ret != SQL_DONE) {
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "master_child: %s", db_errmsg(db));
        sql_finalize(&stmt);
        return false;
    }
    sql_finalize(&stmt);
    return true;
}

// WHERE clause offering only LIVE parents to a FK dropdown / header filter:
// a soft-deleted staff member is not a valid cashier to pick. The fk_where
// filter (e.g. "user_type_dict_id = 'CUSTOMER'") is ANDed in, never replaced.
// Note md_fk_display deliberately does NOT use this gate - see there.
static const char *md_fk_options_where(const MD_Column *col) {
    return col->fk_where
        ? temp_sprintf(" WHERE (%s) AND deleted_at IS NULL", col->fk_where)
        : " WHERE deleted_at IS NULL";
}

static void md_col_load_options(db_t *db, MD_Column *col) {
    if (col == NULL) return;
    if (col->subcols != NULL && col->subcol_count > 0) {
        for (size_t p = 0; p < col->subcol_count; ++p) {
            md_col_load_options(db, &col->subcols[p]);
        }
        return;
    }
    if (col->type != COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT || col->fk_table == NULL) return;
    if (col->fk_cascade) return;
    char *sql = temp_sprintf("SELECT id, %s FROM %s%s ORDER BY %s ASC;",
            col->fk_label, col->fk_table, md_fk_options_where(col),
            col->fk_label);
    sql_stmt stmt = {0};
    if (!sql_prepare(db, sql, &stmt)) {
        return;
    }
    MD_Option *items = NULL;
    size_t count = 0, cap = 0;
    Sql_Step ret;
    for (ret = sql_step(&stmt); ret == SQL_ROW; ret = sql_step(&stmt)) {
        if (count == cap) {
            if (cap == 0) {
                cap = 8;
            } else {
                cap = cap * 2;
            }
            items = realloc(items, cap * sizeof(MD_Option));
        }
        const char *lid = sql_column_text(&stmt, 0);
        if (lid == NULL) {
            items[count].id = temp_strdup("");
        } else {
            items[count].id = temp_strdup(lid);
        }
        const char *l = sql_column_text(&stmt, 1);
        if (l == NULL) {
            items[count].label = temp_strdup("");
        } else {
            items[count].label = temp_strdup(l);
        }
        count++;
    }
    sql_finalize(&stmt);
    col->opt = items;
    col->opt_count = count;
}

// Label for one FK cell. Looks in the (live-only) option list first, then
// falls back to its own ungated query: a row that still points at a
// soft-deleted parent - pre-cascade legacy data, or a parent the fk_where
// filter hides - must render its name, not a raw uuid.
static const char *md_fk_display(db_t *db, const MD_Column *col, const char *id) {
    if (!col || col->type != COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT || !id || !id[0]) return id;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < col->opt_count; ++i) {
        if (strcmp(id, col->opt[i].id) == 0) return col->opt[i].label;
    }
    if (!db || !col->fk_label) return id;
    char *sql = temp_sprintf("SELECT %s FROM %s WHERE id = '%s';",
                             col->fk_label, col->fk_table, md_sql_quote(id));
    sql_stmt stmt = {0};
    if (!sql_prepare(db, sql, &stmt)) return id;
    const char *result = id;
    if (sql_step(&stmt) == SQL_ROW) {
        const char *l = sql_column_text(&stmt, 0);
        if (l && l[0]) result = temp_strdup(l);
    }
    sql_finalize(&stmt);
    return result;
}

static bool md_form_cols_load(db_t *db, const MD_MasterConfig *config,
                              bool lazy_cascade, MD_FormCols *out) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < config->column_count; ++i) {
        MD_FormCol fc = { .col = &config->columns[i] };
        if (fc.col->subcols != NULL && fc.col->subcol_count > 0) {
            for (size_t p = 0; p < fc.col->subcol_count; ++p) {
                md_col_load_options(db, &fc.col->subcols[p]);
            }
        } else if (fc.col->type == COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT && fc.col->fk_table != NULL) {
            bool skip_cascade = false;
            if (fc.col->fk_cascade && lazy_cascade) {
                skip_cascade = true;
            }
            if (!skip_cascade) {
                char *sql = temp_sprintf("SELECT id, %s FROM %s%s ORDER BY %s ASC;",
                        fc.col->fk_label, fc.col->fk_table,
                        md_fk_options_where(fc.col), fc.col->fk_label);
                sql_stmt stmt = {0};
                if (!sql_prepare(db, sql, &stmt)) {
                    return false;
                }
                Sql_Step ret;
                for (ret = sql_step(&stmt); ret == SQL_ROW; ret = sql_step(&stmt)) {
                    MD_Option o = {0};
                    const char *oid = sql_column_text(&stmt, 0);
                    if (oid == NULL) {
                        o.id = temp_strdup("");
                    } else {
                        o.id = temp_strdup(oid);
                    }
                    const char *l = sql_column_text(&stmt, 1);
                    if (l == NULL) {
                        o.label = temp_strdup("");
                    } else {
                        o.label = temp_strdup(l);
                    }
                    da_append(&fc, o);
                }
                sql_finalize(&stmt);
            }
        }
        da_append(out, fc);
    }
    return true;
}

// ---- data query (the Data query tab's search) ---------------------------

// A column the search may cover: every displayed column; hidden internals
// (deleted_at ...) never appear in the scope dropdown. A composite cell
// counts as ONE scope matching any of its parts.
static bool md_col_queryable(const MD_Column *col) {
    return col && !col->hidden;
}

#define MD_MAX_SEARCH_TERMS 8

// One filter term: LIKE '%pattern%' over one queryable column (col), or
// over every displayed column when col == NULL. The per-column filter
// row submits ?q_<col>=<text> -- one term per filled box, ANDed; the
// legacy ?q + ?qcol pair is a single term whose col is NULL when the
// scope is empty or unknown (all-columns fallback).
typedef struct {
    const MD_Column *col;      /* scoped column; NULL = all columns */
    String_View      pattern;  /* "%text%" -- bound to this term's LIKEs */
    int              nbinds;   /* out: LIKE placeholders this term owns */
} MD_SearchTerm;

typedef struct {
    MD_SearchTerm terms[MD_MAX_SEARCH_TERMS];
    size_t        term_count;
} MD_Search;

// Append one ANDed term; the pattern is capped at 100 chars and never
// stored empty, so term_count > 0 is the "searching" test.
static void md_search_add(MD_Search *search, const MD_Column *col,
                          String_View pattern) {
    if (!pattern.count || search->term_count >= MD_MAX_SEARCH_TERMS) return;
    if (pattern.count > 100) pattern.count = 100;
    String_Builder pat = {0};
    sb_append_cstr(&pat, "%");
    sb_append_buf(&pat, pattern.data, pattern.count);
    sb_append_cstr(&pat, "%");
    sb_append_null(&pat);
    MD_SearchTerm *t = &search->terms[search->term_count++];
    t->col = col;
    t->pattern = sv_from_cstr(temp_strdup(pat.items));
    sb_free(pat);
}

static bool md_search_on(const MD_Search *s) {
    return s && s->term_count > 0;
}

// Positional placeholders: $1..$N on postgres, ? elsewhere (bind indexes
// stay 1-based in every driver).
static const char *md_ph(db_t *db, int *n) {
    ++*n;
    return db->lang == SQL_POSTGRES ? temp_sprintf("$%d", *n) : "?";
}

// CAST keeps LIKE type-safe on numeric (and any) columns; mysql spells it
// AS CHAR, sqlite/postgres AS TEXT.
static void md_append_like_cast(String_Builder *sb, db_t *db, const char *expr) {
    sb_append_cstr(sb, "CAST(");
    sb_append_cstr(sb, expr);
    sb_append_cstr(sb, db->lang == SQL_MYSQL
                          ? " AS CHAR) LIKE "
                          : " AS TEXT) LIKE ");
}

static void md_append_col_search(String_Builder *cond, db_t *db,
                                 const char *table_name,
                                 const MD_Column *col, int *n)
{
    if (col->type == COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT && col->fk_table != NULL && col->fk_label != NULL) {
        sb_append_cstr(cond, "(");
        md_append_like_cast(cond, db, col->name);
        sb_append_cstr(cond, md_ph(db, n));
        sb_append_cstr(cond, " OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ");
        sb_append_cstr(cond, col->fk_table);
        sb_append_cstr(cond, " mdq WHERE mdq.deleted_at IS NULL AND mdq.id = ");
        sb_append_cstr(cond, table_name);
        sb_append_cstr(cond, ".");
        sb_append_cstr(cond, col->name);
        sb_append_cstr(cond, " AND ");
        md_append_like_cast(cond, db, temp_sprintf("mdq.%s", col->fk_label));
        sb_append_cstr(cond, md_ph(db, n));
        sb_append_cstr(cond, "))");
    } else {
        md_append_like_cast(cond, db, md_col_sql(col));
        sb_append_cstr(cond, md_ph(db, n));
    }
}

// The whole WHERE for one master view: the soft-delete scope plus the
// table search -- each search term ANDed as its own parenthesized group
// (LIKE over the scoped column, or every displayed one, and for FK
// columns over the label the cell shows: a correlated EXISTS, so "PAID"
// finds its orders without a join). Returns "" or " WHERE ..."; nbinds
// counts LIKE placeholders: bind each term's pattern to the slots it
// owns right after sql_prepare (md_bind_search).
static const char *md_where(db_t *db, const MD_MasterConfig *config,
        bool show_deleted, MD_Search *search,
        int *nbinds)
{
    if (nbinds) *nbinds = 0;
    String_Builder sb = {0};
    const char *joiner = " WHERE ";
    if (config->soft_delete) {
        sb_append_cstr(&sb, show_deleted ? " WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL"
                : " WHERE deleted_at IS NULL");
        joiner = " AND ";
    }
    if (md_search_on(search)) {
        for (size_t t = 0; t < search->term_count; ++t) {
            const MD_SearchTerm *term = &search->terms[t];
            String_Builder cond = {0};
            int n = 0;
            for (size_t ci = 0; ci < config->column_count; ++ci) {
                const MD_Column *col = &config->columns[ci];
                if (!md_col_queryable(col)) continue;
                if (term->col && term->col != col) continue;
                if (cond.count > 0) sb_append_cstr(&cond, " OR ");

                if (col->subcols != NULL && col->subcol_count > 0) {
                    sb_append_cstr(&cond, "(");
                    for (size_t p = 0; p < col->subcol_count; ++p) {
                        if (p > 0) sb_append_cstr(&cond, " OR ");
                        md_append_col_search(&cond, db, config->table, &col->subcols[p], &n);
                    }
                    sb_append_cstr(&cond, ")");
                } else {
                    md_append_col_search(&cond, db, config->table, col, &n);
                }
            }
            if (cond.count) {
                sb_append_cstr(&sb, joiner);
                sb_append_cstr(&sb, "(");
                sb_append_buf(&sb, cond.items, cond.count);
                sb_append_cstr(&sb, ")");
                joiner = " AND ";
            }
            search->terms[t].nbinds = n;
            if (nbinds) *nbinds += n;
            sb_free(cond);
        }
    }
    sb_append_null(&sb);
    char *out = temp_strdup(sb.items);
    sb_free(sb);
    return out;
}

// Bind each term's pattern to the LIKE slots it owns (md_where emits the
// terms' placeholders in order, so the slots run consecutively per term).
// A NULL search (the trash-badge count ignores the filter) has no slots.
static bool md_bind_search(sql_stmt *stmt, const MD_Search *search,
                           int nbinds) {
    if (!search) return true;
    int slot = 1;
    for (size_t t = 0; t < search->term_count && slot <= nbinds; ++t) {
        for (int b = 0; b < search->terms[t].nbinds && slot <= nbinds;
             ++b, ++slot) {
            if (!sql_bind(stmt, slot, SQL_SV(search->terms[t].pattern)))
                return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

static bool md_load_master_with_children(db_t                  *db,
                                         const MD_MasterConfig *config,
                                         MD_MasterRows         *rows,
                                         const Page_Info       *slice,
                                         bool                   show_deleted,
                                         MD_Search             *search)
{
    String_Builder cl = {0};
    sb_append_cstr(&cl, config->id_column);
    for (size_t ci2 = 0; ci2 < config->column_count; ++ci2) {
        const MD_Column *col = &config->columns[ci2];
        if (col->subcols != NULL && col->subcol_count > 0) {
            for (size_t p = 0; p < col->subcol_count; ++p) {
                sb_append_cstr(&cl, ", ");
                sb_append_cstr(&cl, md_col_sql(&col->subcols[p]));
            }
        } else {
            sb_append_cstr(&cl, ", ");
            sb_append_cstr(&cl, md_col_sql(col));
        }
    }
    sb_append_null(&cl);

    int nbinds = 0;
    const char *limit_offset = "";
    if (slice != NULL) {
        limit_offset = temp_sprintf(" LIMIT %zu OFFSET %zu", slice->per_page, slice->offset);
    }
    char *sql = temp_sprintf("SELECT %s FROM %s%s ORDER BY %s DESC%s;",
            cl.items, config->table,
            md_where(db, config, show_deleted, search, &nbinds),
            "created_at",
            limit_offset);
    sql_stmt stmt = {0};
    if (!sql_prepare(db, sql, &stmt)) {
        return false;
    }
    if (!md_bind_search(&stmt, search, nbinds)) {
        sql_finalize(&stmt);
        return false;
    }
    Sql_Step ret;
    for (ret = sql_step(&stmt); ret == SQL_ROW; ret = sql_step(&stmt)) {
        int col_count = sql_column_count(&stmt);
        MD_MasterRow row = {0};
        row.value_count = col_count;
        row.values = malloc(col_count * sizeof(char *));
        row.disp   = malloc(col_count * sizeof(char *));
        for (int i = 0; i < col_count; ++i) {
            row.values[i] = col_to_str(&stmt, i);
            row.disp[i]   = temp_strdup(row.values[i]);
        }
        row.id = row.values[0];
        row.children = malloc(config->children_count * sizeof(MD_ChildRows));
        row.children_count = config->children_count;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < config->children_count; ++ci) {
            row.children[ci].items = NULL;
            row.children[ci].count = 0;
            row.children[ci].capacity = 0;
            if (!load_child_rows(db, &config->children[ci], row.id,
                                 show_deleted, &row.children[ci])) {
                free(row.values);
                for (size_t ci2 = 0; ci2 <= ci; ++ci2) {
                    MD_ChildRows *cr = &row.children[ci2];
                    for (size_t j = 0; j < cr->count; ++j) {
                        free(cr->items[j].values);
                    }
                    free(cr->items);
                }
                free(row.children);
                sql_finalize(&stmt);
                return false;
            }
        }
        da_append(rows, row);
    }
    if (ret != SQL_DONE) {
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "master_child: %s", db_errmsg(db));
        sql_finalize(&stmt);
        return false;
    }
    sql_finalize(&stmt);
    return true;
}

// ---- entry point --------------------------------------------------------

// Total master rows (drives the pager; the window itself is applied by
// md_load_master_with_children's LIMIT/OFFSET).
static bool md_count_masters(db_t *db, const MD_MasterConfig *config,
                             bool show_deleted, MD_Search *search,
                             size_t *out) {
    int nbinds = 0;
    const char *where = md_where(db, config, show_deleted, search, &nbinds);
    char *sql = temp_sprintf("SELECT count(*) FROM %s%s;",
            config->table, where);
    sql_stmt stmt = {0};
    if (!sql_prepare(db, sql, &stmt)) return false;
    bool ok = false;
    if (md_bind_search(&stmt, search, nbinds)
        && sql_step(&stmt) == SQL_ROW) {
        *out = (size_t)sql_column_int64(&stmt, 0);
        ok = true;
    } else {
        nob_log(NOB_ERROR, "master_child count: %s", db_errmsg(db));
    }
    sql_finalize(&stmt);
    return ok;
}

// The per-column filter row: the first <tr> inside the master table's
// header row. Lookup columns (COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT) get a <select> of the
// same choices the add form offers (labels are the query values); plain
// columns get a search input; a composite cell queries its main part
// (col->name == parts[0]) and the placeholder names that part. The last
// cell is submit + clear only -- no box. Inputs post into the empty
// #md-query-form anchor (form attribute) as ?q_<col>=<text>, one ANDed
// term per filled box (md_where).
static void md_query_row(String_Builder *sb, const MD_MasterConfig *config,
                         const MD_FormCols *form_cols, const char *md_path,
                         String_View query, const char *q_text,
                         const char *qcol_name, bool search_active) {
#define OUT(buf, size) sb_append_buf(sb, buf, size);
#define STR(s) sb_append_cstr(sb, s);
#define ESCAPED(s) sb_append_html_escaped(sb, s ? s : "");
#include "build/h_to_html/component/md_child_query_row.h"
#undef OUT
#undef STR
#undef ESCAPED
}

void serve_master_child(Serve_Context *sc, const MD_MasterConfig *config) {
    db_t *db = open_webc_db();
    if (!db) {
        serve_error(sc, 500);
        return;
    }
    // ?fragment=all: load everything, render the bare pagination store
    // (no header/footer) -- the payload js/PaginationSwitcher.js caches.
    bool fragment = page_fragment_requested(sc->query_string);
    // ?nojs=1 - the <noscript> escape hatch on a cascade page: with
    // scripting off GeoCascade.js never fills the village leaf, so a NOT
    // NULL village_id could never be satisfied and staff could not be
    // created at all. Presence of the key makes this render ship the full
    // option list to the CREATE form instead of the lazy cascade (and
    // suppress geo_data, so the template's <noscript> meta refresh is not
    // re-emitted here). The list is deliberately NOT given to the inline
    // update forms: their edit button is JS-only, so that copy would be
    // ~680 KB per row that no no-JS user can ever open.
    // Matched on PRESENCE rather than value: the redirect target is built
    // by appending nojs=1 to a query that may already carry a nojs key,
    // and only presence guarantees that target comes back as "on".
    bool nojs = form_find(sc->query_string, "nojs", NULL);
    bool lazy_cascade = !nojs;
    // The view strip is Live + Trash on a soft_delete page (?deleted=1 =
    // the trash view; no_live hides Live on tables that are never a
    // directly-filled list, and non-soft_delete pages get no strip). The
    // per-column filter row in the table's <thead> (?q_<col> per filled
    // box) filters whichever view is active.
    String_View del_sv = {0};
    bool show_deleted = config->soft_delete
        && form_find(sc->query_string, "deleted", &del_sv)
        && sv_eq(del_sv, sv_from_cstr("1"));
    // Table search: the per-column filter row submits ?q_<col>=<text>
    // per filled box (one ANDed term each); the legacy ?q + ?qcol pair
    // still works as one term. Columns come from this page's config
    // (never interpolated from the URL); every pattern is bound. A qcol
    // that is empty or unknown searches every displayed column.
    String_View q = sv_from_cstr(""), qcol_sv = sv_from_cstr("");
    form_find(sc->query_string, "q", &q);
    form_find(sc->query_string, "qcol", &qcol_sv);
    if (q.count > 100) q.count = 100;
    const char *q_text = q.count
        ? temp_sprintf("%.*s", (int)q.count, q.data) : "";
    const char *qcol_name = "";
    MD_Search search = {0};
    if (q.count > 0) {
        const MD_Column *legacy_col = NULL;
        for (size_t ci = 0; ci < config->column_count; ++ci) {
            const MD_Column *col = &config->columns[ci];
            if (col->name && md_col_queryable(col)
                    && sv_eq(qcol_sv, sv_from_cstr(col->name))) {
                legacy_col = col;
                qcol_name = col->name;
                break;
            }
        }
        md_search_add(&search, legacy_col, q);
    }
    for (size_t ci = 0; ci < config->column_count; ++ci) {
        const MD_Column *col = &config->columns[ci];
        if (!col->name || !md_col_queryable(col)) continue;
        String_View cv = sv_from_cstr("");
        if (form_find(sc->query_string, temp_sprintf("q_%s", col->name), &cv)) {
            md_search_add(&search, col, cv);
        }
    }
    Page_Info page_info = {0}; // master list window
    page_info_parse(sc->query_string, "page", &page_info);
    bool windowed = !fragment;
    if (windowed && !md_count_masters(db, config, show_deleted, &search,
                &page_info.total)) {
        db_close(db);
        serve_error(sc, 500);
        return;
    }
    if (windowed) page_info_finish(&page_info, page_info.total);
    // View strip badge: the trash total (never narrowed by the search).
    size_t trash_total = 0;
    if (config->soft_delete) {
        md_count_masters(db, config, true, NULL, &trash_total);
    }
    // Child tabs share one page key per table (?notes_page=N for every
    // master); totals are per master and computed in the template.
    size_t child_slot_count = config->children_count ? config->children_count : 1;
    Page_Info child_pages[child_slot_count];
    for (size_t ti = 0; ti < config->children_count; ++ti) {
        page_info_parse(sc->query_string,
                temp_sprintf("%s_page", config->children[ti].table),
                &child_pages[ti]);
    }
    MD_MasterRows *rows = md_master_rows_new();
    MD_FormCols form_cols = {0};
    bool ok = md_load_master_with_children(db, config, rows,
            windowed ? &page_info : NULL,
            show_deleted, &search)
        && md_form_cols_load(db, config, lazy_cascade, &form_cols);
    if (ok) {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < config->column_count; ++i) {
            md_col_load_options(db, &config->columns[i]);
        }
        for (size_t ti = 0; ti < config->children_count; ++ti) {
            for (size_t cci = 0; cci < config->children[ti].column_count; ++cci) {
                md_col_load_options(db, &config->children[ti].columns[cci]);
            }
        }
        // FK label substitution into display arrays (slot map: a composite
        // column spans part_count slots whose raw copies already stand in
        // for disp -- its parts are plain fields, never FK labels). Flat
        // date columns humanize here ("05 Oct 2026, 11:56" instead of the
        // raw ISO stamp); values[] keep the raw form for edit prefills.
        for (size_t ri = 0; ri < rows->count; ++ri) {
            MD_MasterRow *r = &rows->items[ri];
            for (size_t ci = 0; ci < config->column_count; ++ci) {
                const MD_Column *col = &config->columns[ci];
                if (col->subcols != NULL && col->subcol_count > 0) {
                    for (size_t p = 0; p < col->subcol_count; ++p) {
                        const MD_Column *scol = &col->subcols[p];
                        size_t slot = md_col_slot(config->columns, ci) + p;
                        if (scol->type == COL_TYPE_DATE) {
                            r->disp[slot] = (char *)md_date_human(r->values[slot]);
                        } else if (scol->type == COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT) {
                            r->disp[slot] = (char *)md_fk_display(db, scol, r->values[slot]);
                        }
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                size_t slot = md_col_slot(config->columns, ci);
                if (col->type == COL_TYPE_DATE) {
                    r->disp[slot] = (char *)md_date_human(r->values[slot]);
                } else {
                    r->disp[slot] = (char *)md_fk_display(db, col, r->values[slot]);
                }
            }
            for (size_t ti = 0; ti < config->children_count; ++ti) {
                const MD_ChildTab *ct = &config->children[ti];
                MD_ChildRows *cr = &r->children[ti];
                for (size_t cj = 0; cj < cr->count; ++cj) {
                    for (size_t cci = 0; cci < ct->column_count; ++cci) {
                        const MD_Column *col = &ct->columns[cci];
                        if (col->subcols != NULL && col->subcol_count > 0) {
                            for (size_t p = 0; p < col->subcol_count; ++p) {
                                const MD_Column *scol = &col->subcols[p];
                                size_t slot = md_col_slot(ct->columns, cci) + p;
                                if (scol->type == COL_TYPE_DATE) {
                                    cr->items[cj].disp[slot] = (char *)md_date_human(cr->items[cj].values[slot]);
                                } else if (scol->type == COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT) {
                                    cr->items[cj].disp[slot] = (char *)md_fk_display(db, scol, cr->items[cj].values[slot]);
                                }
                            }
                            continue;
                        }
                        size_t slot = md_col_slot(ct->columns, cci);
                        if (col->type == COL_TYPE_DATE) {
                            cr->items[cj].disp[slot] = (char *)md_date_human(cr->items[cj].values[slot]);
                        } else {
                            cr->items[cj].disp[slot] = (char *)md_fk_display(db, col, cr->items[cj].values[slot]);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // A fk_cascade column (village_id) renders ancestor navigation selects
    // whose options come from this compact dataset - built while the
    // connection is still open. NULL = no cascade on this page, or the
    // query failed; the template then falls back to the plain select.
    // Suppressed on ?nojs=1: there the plain select IS the full list, and
    // keeping geo_data NULL is also what stops the <noscript> meta
    // refresh from being re-emitted (no redirect loop).
    const char *geo_data = NULL;
    if (!nojs) {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < config->column_count && !geo_data; ++i) {
            if (config->columns[i].fk_cascade) geo_data = md_cascade_json(db, rows, config);
        }
    }
    db_close(db);
    if (!ok) {
        md_master_rows_free(rows);
        serve_error(sc, 500);
        return;
    }
    if (fragment) page_info_finish(&page_info, rows->count);
    String_Builder *sb = &sc->body;
    sb->count = 0;
    // Route path feeds NAV_ACTIVE highlighting in the sidebar and the
    // ?redirect= targets of every mutation form on this page.
    const char *md_path = temp_sprintf("%.*s", (int)sc->uri.count, sc->uri.data);
    // Pager scope contract (see display/component/pagination.h.tt).
    String_View page_query = sc->query_string;
    const char *page_base = md_path;
    const char *page_key = "page";
    const char *page_container = "mc-tbody";
    // Target of the <noscript> meta refresh on a cascade page: this exact
    // URL with nojs=1 appended, preserving page/deleted/q/... so the
    // plain render lands on the same rows the user was looking at.
    const char *nojs_url = sc->query_string.count
        ? temp_sprintf("%s?%.*s&nojs=1", md_path,
                (int)sc->query_string.count, sc->query_string.data)
        : temp_sprintf("%s?nojs=1", md_path);
    if (!fragment) render_page_header(sb, config->title, md_path);
#define OUT(buf, size) sb_append_buf(sb, buf, size);
#define INT(v) sb_append_cstr(sb, temp_sprintf("%zu", v));
#define LLINT(v) sb_append_cstr(sb, temp_sprintf("%lld", v));
#define STR(s) sb_append_cstr(sb, s);
#define ESCAPED(s) sb_append_html_escaped(sb, s ? s : "");
#define PAGE_TITLE(s) sb_append_cstr(sb, s);
#include "build/h_to_html/component/master_child.h"
#undef OUT
#undef INT
#undef LLINT
#undef STR
#undef ESCAPED
#undef PAGE_TITLE
    if (!fragment) render_page_footer(sb);
    md_master_rows_free(rows);
    http_render_response(sc, 200, "text/html", sb_to_sv(*sb));
}

FILE: src/layout/paging.c
