# Decisions

One entry per architectural choice, with the alternatives that lost and why.
Check here before inventing a new pattern.

Convention: this records the decision **as the code embodies it**, with the
rationale that follows from the constraints in
[simplexity.md](simplexity.md). Where the code no longer honours its own
decision, that is said out loud.

---

## D1 — Templates compile to C; there is no template engine in the binary

**Decision.** `display/*.tt` is HTML with `({ C })` islands. `src/tt.c` runs at
build time and emits `build/h_to_html/*.h` containing `OUT("\x..", N);` byte
literals interleaved with the C verbatim. Those headers are `#include`d
*inside* function bodies. See [templates.md](templates.md).

**Why.** The two standard alternatives both cost something real: interpreting
templates at runtime means parsing strings on every request and maintaining a
second language the compiler cannot check; writing HTML as C string literals
means unreadable pages and `\"` escaping everywhere. Compiling removes the
runtime cost entirely and makes the template a typed part of the program.

**Rejected.**

- *Runtime template engine.* Per-request parsing, a second language, and no
  compile-time check that the variables a template names actually exist.
- *HTML as C string literals.* Unwritable past a few lines.
- *A heavier preprocessor / macro DSL.* A second language again, plus the
  maintenance burden of a real compiler.

**Cost.** The generated header only makes sense inside its host function, so a
template cannot be read standalone. And a stale `build/h_to_html/` is
possible if you bypass `build.sh`.

---

## D2 — Coroutines, one per connection, no thread pool

**Decision.** `coroutine_server_run()` accepts on a non-blocking socket and
`coroutine_go(serve_request_coro, fd)` per connection. I/O that would block
returns `-1`/`-2` from `conn_read`/`conn_write`, which the caller turns into
`coroutine_sleep_read/write(fd)` and retries.

**Why.** The retry pattern is uniform and local: every handler is written as
if it were blocking, and the scheduler handles the yield. No handler shares
state with any other, so there is nothing to lock.

**Rejected.**

- *Thread per connection.* Stack memory per client plus locking around the
  DB pool, for no gain on a single-process app.
- *Thread pool.* Pool size becomes a hard concurrency limit and handlers must
  tolerate blocking the pool's threads.
- *fork per connection.* No shared connection pool, and the lazy pool
  (`pool_grow()` on first use) would be pointless.
- *epoll with an explicit state machine.* The classic scalable answer — and
  it turns every handler into a callback chain. Reads worse for the same
  scale.

**Cost.** Blocking calls inside a handler stall its coroutine (and only its
coroutine), but nothing catches that for you.

---

## D3 — A static route table with three match kinds

**Decision.** `route.c` builds one array at first use. Entries are
`ROUTE_EXACT`, `ROUTE_PREFIX`, or `ROUTE_ID_ACTION` (`/<prefix>/<id>/<suffix>`),
scanned linearly, with an optional method per entry (`NULL` = the handler
dispatches).

**Why.** Twenty-odd routes do not justify a trie or a regex engine, and a
linear scan over an array is the shortest code that cannot be wrong.
`ROUTE_ID_ACTION` centralises id extraction so handlers never re-parse the
URI, and `parse_uri_id()` classifies all-digits segments as `ID_INT` for
legacy integer keys.

**Rejected.**

- *Hand-written if/else chain per route.* Differs per route, so adding one
  means re-reading the whole chain to place it correctly.
- *Regex router.* Allocation and failure modes per request, and the
  backreference semantics are a common source of bugs.
- *Trie/prefix tree.* Real complexity for a table this size.

**Cost.** Linear scan — irrelevant at this size, but it is not a scaling
answer. Order matters and nothing enforces that a `ROUTE_PREFIX` is not
shadowed by an earlier exact route.

---

## D4 — Postgres is an honest stub while the dialect stays first-class

**Decision.** Every `[SQL_POSTGRES]` entry — query tables, DDL, migrations —
exists. `driver_postgres.c` is a complete `Sql_Driver` vtable whose every
function fails, and `pg_drv_open()` writes
`"postgres driver is not implemented yet"` into `db->err`.

**Why.** It fails at the single cheapest point — `db_open()` — with a sentence
that names the problem. Every alternative fails later and more expensively.

**Rejected.**

- *Drop Postgres from the schema layer until it is implemented.* Then
  implementing it later means rewriting every query table and every migration,
  because the dialect axis would have been removed.
- *Pretend to connect.* Fails somewhere obscure, likely with a misleading
  error, or worse returns wrong results.
- *Leave it half-wired without a message.* A silent `false` from `prepare()`
  with no text is the worst of both.

**Cost.** `WEBC_DB=postgres:...` looks supported in the docs table and is not.
Mitigated by saying so in [README.md](../README.md), [database.md](database.md)
and here.

---

## D5 — Migration history stores the exact SQL text

**Decision.** `Migrations(applied_at, query)` stores the full text of each
applied migration. On every open, stored text is compared with the current
files, byte for byte, and a difference is `SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH`. The
compare is **order-independent** — every stored row must equal some
`migrations[]` entry and vice versa — because the table has no key to order
by, and row order differs per dialect (MySQL hidden PK, Postgres arbitrary).

**Why.** A version number cannot detect that an *already applied* migration was
edited — which is the actual way people break their databases. Storing the text
turns silent corruption into a detectable state, and lets the backup/restore
path (`db.bak` → fresh migrate → copy shared tables) run automatically.

**Rejected.**

- *Version number only.* Blind to edits; the app then runs against a schema
  nobody validated.
- *Hash of the file.* Detects a difference but tells you nothing about what
  differs — you cannot print `EXPECTED:` / `FOUND:` as the error does.
- *No history, just `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`.* Cannot apply anything after
  the first version.

**Cost.** Editing a shipped migration file breaks every existing database —
which is exactly what `test/golden/` exists to prevent. When the edit is
deliberate, the golden is re-pinned to the new bytes **in the same commit**
(the `0003_pos_eshop` `v_geo_hierarchy` amend, 2026-11-05); a new numbered
migration is the right tool only when no deployed database carries the old
bytes. See [testing.md](testing.md).

---

## D6 — One translation unit per `.c` file; never unity-include a `.c`

**Decision.** `nob.c` globs every `.c` under `src/` (excluding `tt.c` and
`nob.c`) and compiles each once. Files are shared through `.h` only. Nothing
in `src/` may `#include "*.c"`.

**Why.** The glob means a new `.c` compiles automatically with no list to
update — that is the whole point of globbing. But a file that is *also*
included as text by another source is compiled twice, and the linker reports
`multiple definition of ...`.

**Rejected.**

- *Explicit source list in `nob.c`.* No duplicate-symbol hazard, but every new
  file needs a manual edit, and a forgotten entry fails silently as an
  undefined reference.
- *Unity builds.* Deliberately opposite: faster builds, but every symbol in
  the unity blob shares one TU, so `static` stops meaning file-scope and
  include order starts changing behaviour.

**This regression happened here.** `src/user/user.c` and `src/notes/notes.c`
carried four unity-includes of `.c` files, and the link failed with duplicate
`render_page_header` / `render_page_footer`. The fix was to revert those four
to the matching `.h` — restoring the decision, not working around it.

**Cost.** No compile-time merging; the glob's exclusion list must be kept
current when a file must not be compiled directly.

---

## D7 — `Connection: close` on every response

**Decision.** `http_render_response()` always writes
`Connection: close`, and `serve_request_coro` shuts down and closes after one
response.

**Why.** Keep-alive requires connection-reuse state in a scheduler that has
none: parsing pipelined requests, tracking which response belongs to which
request, idle timeouts, and half-closed sockets. With one response per
connection, teardown is unconditional and provable — the drain-then-close
sequence in the cleanup path exists for exactly one case.

**Rejected.**

- *Keep-alive (HTTP/1.1 default).* Real throughput win for a browser fetching
  many assets, at the cost of a state machine the scheduler does not have.
- *HTTP/1.0-style request-response with reuse negotiated.* Same problem.

**Cost.** A new TCP connection per asset. For a local/single-user app this is
noise; at scale it is the first thing to change — and the two places that must
change together are the response builder and the `cleanup` path
(see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).

---

## D8 — Static assets are embedded, with a disk fallback

**Decision.** `nob.c` bakes `css/output.css`, two images and the four JS files
into `build/bundle.h` as `bundle[]` + a `resources[]` table.
`serve_resource()` looks the path up there first, and only reads from disk if
it is not bundled.

**Why.** The binary runs standalone — no asset directory to ship, and no
"works in the repo, 404s when deployed" failure. The disk fallback covers what
cannot be known at build time, notably uploaded avatars.

**Rejected.**

- *Disk only.* The app then depends on its working directory, and a missing
  `css/output.css` at runtime is a silent blank page.
- *Bundle only.* Uploaded files cannot be bundled; would have forced a second
  serving path anyway.

**Cost.** A full rebuild is required to pick up a CSS or JS edit — which is
also why `dev_visit_file` explicitly excludes `css/output.css` from the
rebuild trigger, so a Tailwind output write does not immediately retrigger its
own build.

---

## D9 — Refuse to open a database whose schema is newer than the code

**Decision.** In `create_schema_status()`, if `Migrations` holds more rows than
`migrations[]` has entries:

```c
ERROR: <path>: Database scheme is too new. Contains more migrations applied
than expected. Update your application.
```

→ `SCHEMA_ERROR`, the open fails, and the pool **latches** on that first
use: it stays dead for the process, `db_pool_get()` returns `NULL`
immediately (one log line, no per-request retry), and the server keeps
listening; DB-backed routes return 500. Nothing is opened before a request
asks for the database, so the refusal happens at first use, not at startup.

**Why.** The application genuinely does not know the schema it would be
running against — columns, tables and constraints exist that no query in this
binary was written for. Silently ignoring the unknown migrations would run
half the app against a schema it does not understand, and *that* failure mode
hides data damage. Failing loudly at open, with a message that says what to do
("update your application"), is the honest outcome. Note this is a different
path from D5's `SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH`, which **is** recoverable
automatically — an unknown *count* is not, because the code has no
corresponding expectation to restore against.

**Rejected.**

- *Ignore extra migrations and open anyway.* The code would issue queries
  against tables it never declared; failures would be scattered and misleading.
- *Truncate / roll back the history.* Destructive to a database the user may
  have real data in — and it would throw away information about what the
  schema actually is.
- *Best-effort downgrade.* No such thing exists for arbitrary DDL.

**Cost.** A database migrated by a newer or different checkout of this project
becomes unopenable by this one, and the failure surfaces as 500s on DB routes
rather than a refusal to start. The live `~/sqlite3/webc_c/db` is healthy —
11 history rows matching the 11 registered migrations (verified 2026-11-04);
the failure mode is analysed in [dev-log.md](dev-log.md).

---

## D10 — The migration registry is a compile-time array

**Decision.** `migrations[]` in `db.c` names each migration directory and its
three dialect files. Files on disk that are absent from the array never run.

**Why.** The set of applied migrations must be reproducible and reviewable in
the diff. A compile-time array also lets `migration_sql(index)` index straight
into it for the byte-for-byte comparison in D5, and gives `ARRAY_LEN(migrations)`
as the expected count.

**Rejected.**

- *Scan `migrations/` at runtime.* Order becomes filesystem-dependent unless
  the sort is careful, adding a migration is invisible in review, and the
  expected count becomes an artifact of the deploy rather than the binary.
- *Embedding the SQL as C strings.* What the code had before; D5's note in
  `db.c` records that `sqlite3.sql` files must still match those old inline
  strings byte for byte, because existing databases hold them.

**Cost.** Adding a migration is two steps — directory *and* array entry — and
forgetting the second means it silently never applies.

---

## D11 — SQLite is the default; the dialect is a prefix on `WEBC_DB`

**Decision.** No config file. `main()` resolves four environment variables
once, before anything touches the database:

1. `WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL` (`SQLITE3` / `MYSQL` / `POSTGRES`, case-insensitive) —
   an explicit dialect that **overrides prefix detection**;
2. `WEBC_DB` — the full DSN or file path (wins for the location);
3. `WEBC_CONNECTION_STRING` — a raw DSN, read only when `WEBC_DB` is unset;
4. `WEBC_DEFAULT_DSN` — the compiled-in constant in `src/webc.c`, the one
   place to edit the connection string (this checkout ships it as
   `~/sqlite3/webc_c/db`; a leading `~/` expands to `$HOME` because the DSN
   never passes through a shell);
5. nothing at all → **no connection is ever attempted**; DB routes answer
   "no database configured". There is no baked `$HOME` fallback.

The three globals the resolution used to write (`WEBC_DB_PATH`,
`WEBC_DIR_PATH`, `WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL`) are macros over one set-once `Db_Cfg`
struct in `db.h` - assigned in `main()`, read-only afterwards.

`webc_db_lang()` then answers: the pin if set, else a `mysql:`/`postgres:`
prefix on `WEBC_DB_PATH`, else SQLite (anything else is a file path).
`webc_open_db_spec()` applies the same rule per spec string, so an explicit
prefix on a second database's spec wins even under a pin.

**Why.** SQLite needs no server, credentials or daemon, so a clone builds and
runs with nothing configured — the smallest possible onboarding. One variable
selects both the dialect and the location, so there is exactly one thing to
set; the pin exists for the opposite case (a dialect that must not be guessed
from a path), and `WEBC_CONNECTION_STRING` for callers that think in DSNs.

**Rejected.**

- *Config file.* A second source of truth to keep in sync with the
  environment, and a file that must exist before `help` can run.
- *`--dialect` flag plus `--db`.* Two arguments that must agree; `mysql:` with
  a file path is a combination that has no meaning.
- *MySQL default.* Requires a running daemon — the project would not run on a
  fresh clone at all.
- *`WEBC_CONNECTION_STRING` above `WEBC_DB`.* The test harness (and every
  documented example) sets `WEBC_DB`; flipping the order would silently
  redirect them.

**Cost.** No way to discover a dialect from the path alone, and the parent
directory of a SQLite `WEBC_DB` silently becomes the "webc dir" that
legacy-file logic operates on — for a `mysql:`/`postgres:` DSN there is no
directory to derive, so `WEBC_DIR_PATH` becomes `.`.

---

## D12 — No `-std=` is pinned

**Recorded as-is.** The build invokes `cc` with `-Wall -Wextra -Wswitch-enum`
and no `-std=`, so the standard is whatever the compiler defaults to. On this
machine (GCC 16.2.1) that is `__STDC_VERSION__ 202311L` — C23.

**Why it reads like an omission, not a decision.** Nothing in the tree
justifies it, and `-Wswitch-enum` *is* pinned, so standards discipline exists
in a neighbouring line. Left as D12 rather than silently "fixed" because
pinning a standard changes what the compiler accepts and deserves its own
build-and-test run — the same reasoning as the `tt` escape note in
[templates.md](templates.md).

**Rejected (should it be pinned).**

- *`-std=c11`.* Portable, but would need auditing against what the code
  actually uses today.
- *`-std=gnu11`* / *`gnu17`.* Fixes a dialect while keeping GNU extensions,
  which the code does not obviously rely on.

**Cost.** The same tree compiles as different dialects on different compilers,
so "works on my machine" cannot be assumed for standard-dependent behaviour.

## D13 — One `src/` tree, `third_party/` for vendored code, `nob.c` at the root

**Decision (2026-10-19).** Mirror the sibling `webc` project's layout: a single
`src/` tree holding every first-party module (`http`, `layout`, `auth`, `i18n`,
`report`, `notes`, `user`, `people`, `version`, `pos`, `shop`, `helper`,
`dashboard`, `crud`, `db`, `core/webc_template.h`, `webc.c`, `tt.c`); vendored
dependencies under `third_party/` (`coroutine/`, `nob/`,
`sqlite-amalgamation-3460100/`); and the build driver `nob.c` at the project
root instead of `nob.c`.

**Why.** The old tree split the same concerns across `core/*` (http, auth,
i18n, report, layout, display) and `src/*` (entities, db), with vendored code
in `module/`. A reader had to know that `core/display/notes.c` and
`src/notes/` were two halves of one entity. Collapsing to one `src/` tree — and
merging split entities (`notes`, `user`) into one file each — makes the
directory listing self-explanatory and matches the reference project.

**Consequences.**

- Build globs only `src/**.c` (the `core` dir is gone). New modules are one
  directory + one `route_new` line, no engine edits.
- Includes were rewritten `module/`→`third_party/`, `core/*`→`src/*`. Two
  leftover guard names (`CORE_SERVE_H_`, `PEOPLE_H_`) are cosmetic.
- The `webc.c` `dev` watcher and its SQLite exclusion still name the *old*
  paths (`core`, `nob.c`, `module/…`) — documented as known gaps in
  [cli.md](cli.md), not silently "fixed" here.

**Rejected.**

- *Keep `core/` + `src/` split.* Familiar to this repo's history, but the
  split is the very thing that obscured which file owned an entity.
- *Move the build driver under `src/`.* Would drop it into the compile glob;
  the root is where `webc` keeps it and where the glob can exclude it by name.

## D14 — Route both PDF and DOCX reports through FODT for page-style chrome

**Decision (2026-10-19).** Downloadable reports always convert
`html → flat ODT (fodt) → {pdf,docx}`, never `html → pdf` directly. The
running header/footer (letterhead, dividers, "PAGE X-Y") are injected as an
ODF page-style `<style:header>`/`<style:footer>` on the body's `HTML`
master-page in the intermediate FODT, so LibreOffice repeats them on every
printed page and fills the live page-number fields at layout time.

**Why.** The old PDF path opened the HTML as Writer/Web, which has **no
page-style headers/footers and no page-number fields** — it is a single flowing
web document, so a repeated letterhead and "Page X of Y" are impossible there.
A Writer (flat ODT) document is the only LibreOffice model that carries
per-page chrome; routing PDF through it too means one code path serves both
formats instead of two divergent ones. Page numbers *must* come from ODF
fields: the C code emits one blob and never knows how it will paginate, so a
static count in the struct cannot work.

**Consequences.**

- `report_convert` always does the FODT detour (3 soffice steps for PDF, which
  was 1 before) — a few extra hundred ms on an already-async download.
- `report_fodt_decorate()` owns the chrome: it injects header/footer styles
  into `<office:automatic-styles>` and expands the self-closing `HTML`
  master-page. `rfooter` is injected as ODF markup (it embeds the
  `PAGE_CURR`/`PAGE_LAST` fields); the other five chrome strings are
  XML-escaped text.
- The table's grid / dark header / zebra are emitted as **presentational HTML
  attributes** (`border`, `bgcolor`, `<font color>`), because the html→FODT
  import drops CSS backgrounds and cell borders (only paragraph properties
  survive). The header/footer bands are 3-column borderless **tables**, not
  tab stops, so a multi-line cell (the 2-line shop header) still lines up.

**Rejected.**

- *Keep the direct `html → pdf` Writer/Web path for speed.* Cheaper, but it
  cannot repeat a header/footer or number pages — the whole point of this
  change. The FODT detour is the only way to get standard-document chrome.
- *Statically compute page numbers in C.* Impossible: pagination happens
  inside LibreOffice at layout time, after the blob is emitted. Hence live
  `<text:page-number>`/`<text:page-count>` fields.
- *Style the table with CSS.* The html→FODT import silently discards CSS
  backgrounds and borders (leaving an invisible white-on-white header row and
  no grid), so presentational attributes are the reliable channel.


=====================================================
FILE: wiki/testing.md

# Testing

How the app runs against a database nobody cares about.

## The one rule

> **No test can touch a real database.**

`test/run.sh` exports a throwaway `HOME` before anything starts and every
test sets `WEBC_DB` explicitly, which wins over the compiled-in
`WEBC_DEFAULT_DSN` — so the real database is never opened. If a test ever
reaches your real data, the harness is broken — treat that as a bug in the
harness first.

## `test/run.sh`

```bash
./test/run.sh              # build, then run everything
SKIP_BUILD=1 ./test/run.sh # reuse the current build/bin/webc
```

### What it does, in order

1. **Build**, unless `SKIP_BUILD` is set. Failure prints the last 30 lines of
   `/tmp/webc_test_build.log` and exits 1 — you never get a red test run
   caused by a stale binary without being told.
2. **Isolate.** `TMP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/webc_test.XXXXXX)`, then:
   ```bash
   export HOME="$TMP"
   export WEBC_DB="$TMP/nested/deep/db"   # recursive mkdir is part of the test
   ```
   `HOME` is redirected because that is where the default DB path comes from.
   `WEBC_DB` deliberately points at a path whose parents do not exist, so
   directory creation is exercised on every run.
3. **Pick a free port** by binding a socket to port 0 from Python — no fixed
   port, so runs cannot collide with each other or with a running server.
4. **Start the server**: `./build/bin/webc serve "$PORT" > "$TMP/server.log"`.
5. **Run the suites** (see below).
6. **`trap cleanup EXIT`** — always tears down, even on failure:
   - kill the server
   - remove every upload file recorded by the suite in `$TMP/uploads.txt`
   - `rmdir resource/image/upload`
   - `rm -rf "$TMP"`

### Suite orchestration

```bash
python3 test/mysql_test.py "$TMP"  > "$TMP/mysql_test.log"  2>&1 &   # background
python3 test/https_test.py "$TMP"  > "$TMP/https_test.log"  2>&1 &   # background
python3 test/http_test.py "$HOST" "$PORT" "$TMP"                     # foreground
python3 test/crud_contract_test.py "$HOST" "$PORT" "$TMP"            # after http_test
python3 test/geo_cascade_test.py "$HOST" "$PORT" "$TMP"              # real browser
python3 test/img_upload_test.py "$HOST" "$PORT" "$TMP"               # real browser
[ -n "$MYSQL_PID" ] && wait "$MYSQL_PID"; [ -n "$HTTPS_PID" ] && wait "$HTTPS_PID"
cat "$TMP/mysql_test.log" "$TMP/https_test.log"   # only when the suite ran
```

The SQLite suite runs against the shared server on the foreground; the dialect
and TLS suites run **in parallel**, each with its **own** server, `mariadbd` or
cert. All state lives under `$TMP`, so the single cleanup trap covers all
three.

Exit code is sticky — any suite failing sets `rc=1` and the other suites still
finish. You get every failure in one run rather than one at a time.

## The suites

| Suite | Server | Backend | Skips when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http_test.py` | shared (`$HOST:$PORT`) | SQLite (`$WEBC_DB`) | never |
| `crud_contract_test.py` | shared (after `http_test`) | SQLite | never |
| `geo_cascade_test.py` | shared (after the contract suite) | SQLite | no chromium, or python `websocket` missing |
| `img_upload_test.py` | shared (after geo) | SQLite | no chromium, or python `websocket` missing |
| `mysql_test.py` | own | throwaway `mariadbd` | webc built without libmariadb, or MariaDB tooling missing |
| `https_test.py` | own, TLS | own throwaway SQLite DB | webc built without openssl, or `openssl` CLI missing |

**Skip = exit 0 with a printed reason.** A missing optional tool — or an
optional dependency that was absent on the *build* host (nob.c's feature
gateway records it in `build/webc_features.h`, which `run.sh` and both suite
entry points read) — is not a failure, so the suite stays green on a machine
without MariaDB or OpenSSL — but it also means **a green run does not prove
those suites ran**. Check the logs if coverage matters.

### `http_test.py` — main suite

The bulk of coverage (~19 KB). Runs against the shared server on the chosen
free port, and records every upload file it creates into `$TMP/uploads.txt` so
the cleanup trap can delete them.

### `mysql_test.py` — dialect proof

Boots a private `mariadbd` with:

- a throwaway datadir under `$TMP`
- a unix socket (no networking)
- `--skip-networking`

then starts a webc pointed at it with
`WEBC_DB='mysql:user=root;password=;database=webc;socket=...'`, runs the HTTP
checks, and **verifies the resulting rows through the `mariadb` CLI** — so it
confirms what actually landed in the server, not what the app thinks it wrote.
Both are torn down at exit.

### `https_test.py` — TLS proof

Generates a throwaway self-signed certificate, boots its own server with
`WEBC_TLS_CERT` + `WEBC_TLS_KEY` and its own SQLite DB, then checks:

- pages load over TLS
- a form POST lands
- **plaintext on the TLS port is not served as HTTP** — the property that
  `tls_server_init()` aborting on misconfiguration is supposed to guarantee,
  verified end to end

## `test/golden/`

Golden files pin the migration SQL **byte for byte**, most importantly the
`sqlite3.sql` files.

Why this matters: an already-applied migration's exact text is stored in the
`Migrations.query` column and re-compared on every open. Editing a shipped
migration file is therefore a `SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH` for every existing
database. The golden test turns "someone tidied up a migration" into a red
test instead of a data-loss incident for users. See
[database.md](database.md).

When a shipped migration is edited *deliberately*, re-pin the golden to the
new bytes *in the same commit* — that is what `0003_pos_eshop.sqlite3.sql`
received on 2026-11-05 (the `v_geo_hierarchy` view; adding a new numbered
migration instead would have forced a D5 rebuild of every deployed database).

## Layout

```
test/
  run.sh          harness: build, isolate, spawn, run, teardown
  testlib.py      Checker — assertion helper shared by the suites
  http_test.py    SQLite suite (main)
  crud_contract_test.py  form/handler contract (runs after http_test)
  geo_cascade_test.py    real-browser suite for GeoCascade.js
  img_upload_test.py     real-browser suite for ImageUpload.js (preview,
                         crop modal, compression; skips without chromium)
  mysql_test.py   MariaDB suite (own server + own mariadbd)
  https_test.py   TLS suite (own cert + own server)
  golden/         pinned migration files
  __pycache__/    disposable
```

## Adding a test

1. `from testlib import Checker` and follow the existing suites' shape.
2. Take `$TMP` from `sys.argv` for anything you create — never a path outside
   it, or the cleanup trap will not remove it.
3. Record created upload files in `$TMP/uploads.txt`.
4. If the test needs tooling, **skip with exit 0** and say why; do not fail.
5. If it introduces a migration, add the file *and* the `migrations[]` entry,
   then update `test/golden/`.

## What is not covered

Honest gaps, kept in [dev-log.md](dev-log.md) as well:

- **No Postgres suite** — the driver is a stub, so there is nothing to run.
- **No concurrency test.** The pool's checkout tracking, transient-fallback
  and release rollback (see [database.md](database.md)) are untested; no suite
  opens more than one request at a time.
- **`src/crud/` is untested** because it is untested *and* unreferenced — no
  caller exists to drive it.
- **No keep-alive or chunked-encoding test** — neither is implemented.

# webc_c — State Wiki (reference)

> Why: project state too large to keep in conversation. Keep this current.
> Repo: /mnt/disk2/mythings/study_my_code/c/webc_c (git repo root is the parent
> c/; sibling webc/ is an older copy — ignore it).

## What this is
C + SQLite/MySQL/Postgres-stub web CRUD app (demo evolving into a POS/e-shop
admin). Custom build (nob), custom template compiler (tt), no framework,
vanilla JS only.

## Build / test
- Build: ./build/bin/nob (compiled from root ./nob.c) -> build/bin/webc. New .c
  files under src/ are auto-globbed — no build edits needed (only new
  js/css/images need a root nob.c resources[] entry).
- Run: webc serve [port], webc dev [port] (auto rebuild+reload); env
  WEBC_DB / WEBC_CONNECTION_STRING (location, DB wins), WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL
  (dialect pin), WEBC_TLS_CERT/WEBC_TLS_KEY (both or nothing).
- Tests: ./test/run.sh (builds; throwaway HOME+WEBC_DB under /tmp; never
  touches real DB). SKIP_BUILD=1 to reuse build. Suites: http_test.py (sqlite),
  crud_contract_test.py, geo_cascade_test.py + img_upload_test.py (real
  chromium; skip without it), mysql_test.py (own mariadbd), https_test.py.
  Baseline before POS work: **140 passing (94 + 40 + 6)**.
- Real DB ~/sqlite3/webc_c/db — NEVER write to it from tests/tools.

## master_child engine (key facts)
- MD_MasterConfig{table,title,id_column,crud_path,columns,sum,children[]};
  MD_Column{name,label,type,nullable,fk_*,subcols,subcol_count,style,read_sql,choices,hidden,computed}.
- Types: COL_TYPE_TEXT, COL_TYPE_NUM, COL_TYPE_DATE, COL_TYPE_TEXTAREA, COL_TYPE_FK_SELECT, COL_TYPE_IMG, COL_TYPE_COMPOSITE.
- Composite cells use nested MD_Column sub-columns via Pattern 2 macros: MD_FIELD, MD_FK, MD_CHOICE, MD_STACK, MD_AVATAR, MD_ACTIVITY. No parallel MD_Cell struct.
- Sub-columns support independent foreign keys (dictionaries/orgs), choices, and nullability. Engine recurses into subcols for option loading, FK label resolution, and multi-field search filtering.
- Master: SQL window (LIMIT/OFFSET) + count(*); children loaded fully and windowed in template. ORDER BY created_at DESC.
- Forms: form="..." attr wiring (edit mdf-e-<table>-<id>, add mdf-a-<table>-<masterid>); md_fk_display() swaps FK ids -> labels after load for both flat columns and sub-columns.

## Directory map
- third_party/ — vendored deps: coroutine/, nob/nob.h, sqlite-amalgamation-3460100/.
- nob.c (project root) — the build driver (was nob.c). Globs only src/**.c.
- src/http/ — serve.c (hang fix), route.c (route_initialize(): one route_new
  line per page), utils.h (form_find), serve.h (sb_append_html_escaped), id.h.

  paging.c/.h = Page_Info pagination core, dashboard.c = / landing.
- src/core/webc_template.h — SERVE_READ/EDIT/CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/CRUD macros
  (per-module glue, NOT a generic CRUD layer).
- src/{notes,user,people,version}/ — demo/entity modules. notes.c/.h and
  user.c/.h are single merged files (data + controller + render, webc style);
  people.c = /people composition example.
- src/auth/ (login/signup/session), src/i18n/ (request-bound lang state),
  src/report/ (report registry {id, khmer_title, sql,...}).

  payments, ... one .c/.h per entity).

  driver_postgres=stub), db.c = migrations.
- src/crud/ — declarative CRUD API, **compiled, zero callers** (dead leftover).
- src/webc.c (CLI entry), src/tt.c (template compiler, build-time only).
- display/ — .tt templates (build/bin/tt -> build/h_to_html/** hex-escaped C
  OUT("...") literals). ({ C code }) = raw inline C, else literal HTML.

  vs inline HTML: templates.md "When to template vs inline".
- js/ — ListExpandSwitcher.js (smart master_child: snapshot->fetch->swap->
  reveal), PaginationSwitcher.js (fragment-store paging), sidebarSwitcher,
  themeSwitcher, ImageUpload.js (photo preview/crop/compress, wired by the
  [data-img-upload] wrapper). Bundled via root nob.c resources[].
- test/ — run.sh, http_test.py, crud_contract_test.py, geo_cascade_test.py,
  img_upload_test.py, mysql_test.py, https_test.py, testlib.py
  (Client, Checker, db_query = scalar, db_exec), golden/ byte-exact pins.
- migrations/000N_name/{sqlite3,mysql,postgres}.sql — per-dialect, applied in
  ONE transaction => NO PRAGMAs inside files (connection PRAGMAs run in
  sqlite_drv_open()); sqlite files byte-exact for existing DBs (golden-pinned);
  list = static migrations[] in src/db/db.c; golden check list hardcoded in
  http_test.py (~line 85: 0001_notes, 0002_users, 0003_pos_eshop).

## Hard rules (user)
- NO generic CRUD layer; NO sql_each — inline sql_step loops with column++.
- Adding a page/module = own file + one route_new line, zero engine edits.
- Reusable types in master_child.h/.c stay stable (interface directive).
- JS: vanilla only; server byte-identical with JS disabled (no-JS PRG path).
  Narrow exception, Phase 27: `?nojs=1` renders the full village list for the
  cascade CREATE form, reached only via a `<noscript>` meta refresh (see
  Phase 27). No user-agent sniffing - the URL is the only signal.
- Style: compact, information-dense, NO modern styling; keep px-0.5 py-1.5
  inputs; do NOT use radius/padding/margin to express nesting — hierarchy via
  BACKGROUND COLOR STEPS (light white/gray-50/gray-100/200; dark
  gray-900/800/700) + hairline borders/dividers.
- README.md belongs to the user — do not touch.

## Pagination contract (shipped, tested)
- SSR first window via SQL LIMIT/OFFSET + count; Page_Info (src/layout/
  paging.h); clamps page->[1,total_pages], per_page->[1,100] (default 20),
  page=abc -> 1.
- Nav ALWAYS renders (1 page => Prev/Next disabled spans); attrs
  data-pg-container|key|base|per; page links carry data-pg-n, per-page links
  carry none (always SSR reload).
- Prefetch ?fragment=all (no doctype, has id="pg-store", <template
  data-pg-pager="<container>" data-pg-n="N">); armed only when a real
  data-pg-n link exists. JS slices store by data-pg-unit child groups
  (users/notes=1, master cluster=3, child row=3 incl its <form>), preserves
  tr.md-add-row, purges nested stores after master flip, patchCluster syncs
  holder, window.pgReset/pgArm hooked into mdSwap.
- Row-group units: child row = [md-row tr, edit tr, form] = 3 tbody children;
  master cluster = [display tr, edit tr, panel tr] = 3.

## Phase 22 - Cache-Control: no-store fixes stale table after CRUD (suite 880 PASS)
- Root cause of "the table only updates after a manual reload or
  route change": every response carried
  `Last-Modified: WEBC_BUILD_TIME` with no Cache-Control, so browsers
  applied RFC 9111 heuristic freshness (10% of the binary's age --
  hours for a days-old build). The CRUD fetch follows the server's
  normal POST -> 302 -> GET chain, that GET hit the heuristic-fresh
  cache entry, and mdSwap() swapped the STALE page's #mc-root back
  into the DOM: edits/deletes never appeared until a real reload.
- Fix: http_render_response (+ _attachment) now send
  `Cache-Control: no-store` and drop the bogus Last-Modified stamp
  (every response is dynamic: session, DB, per-user data; static
  assets are bundle-embedded). ListExpandSwitcher's fetch also passes
  cache: 'no-store' as belt and braces.
- Tests: + header pin (no-store, no Last-Modified on a list page).
  Suite: 880 PASS (http 120 / pos 377 / shop 118 / role 48 /
  crud_contract 170 / mysql 41 / https 6).

## Phase 23 - Duplicate unique values -> 409 with a reason (suite 881 PASS)
- A UNIQUE rejection (duplicate code/sku/pair ...) surfaced as a generic
  HTTP 500 "Request failed" banner -- e.g. creating a category with an
  existing cat_code. A user mistake, not a crash.
- SERVE_CREATE/SERVE_UPDATE copy the driver message BEFORE the rollback
  (a successful rollback resets sqlite/mysql last-error state), detect
  the dialect's unique wording via db_msg_is_unique() (sqlite
  "UNIQUE constraint failed", mysql "Duplicate entry", postgres
  "duplicate key value"), and answer 409 text/plain with
  "A <singular> with the same unique value already exists. (<driver msg>)".
- mdBanner (ListExpandSwitcher) takes an optional reason: the fetch
  error path shows a plain-text response body as the banner text, so the
  user reads WHAT collided instead of "HTTP 500"; styled HTML error
  pages keep the generic message (only Content-Type: text/plain is
  surfaced).
- Tests: duplicate cat_code pin (409 + reason in body); the three former
  duplicate->500 pins (deliveries / role_permissions / translations)
  flipped to 409. Suite: 881 PASS (http 120 / pos 378 / shop 118 /
  role 48 / crud_contract 170 / mysql 41 / https 6).

## Phase 24 - create_only flag + writable /pos/dictionaries (suite 892 PASS)
- New MD_MasterConfig flag create_only (the inverse of no_create): the
  generic add form stays, the row actions (edit/delete/restore) hide,
  and the module registers ONLY the /create route. First user:
  /pos/dictionaries -- staff can append lookup rows (category / code /
  label, sort defaults to 0) but not edit or delete the shared dict.
- Template: master_child.h.tt gates the edit BUTTON, the inline edit
  ROW (previously rendered unconditionally -- even on read_only
  pages), the delete form and the restore form with !create_only.
- pos.c: create_pos_dict (3-dialect INSERT; sort_order binds pos_num
  so an empty box stores the column default 0) + SERVE_CREATE(pos_dict,
  pos_dict, ...); the page fn is serve_pos_dict; pos.h and route.c
  follow (GET /pos/dictionaries + POST /pos/dictionaries/create only).
- Tests: the dictionaries read_only block became the create-only block
  (add form present, no edit/delete/restore, create -> 302 + row +
  sort 0, duplicate UNIQUE(category, code) -> 409 + reason,
  /update /delete /restore -> 404). crud_contract learned to skip the
  update/delete legs on create-only pages (row located by data-row-id,
  not the update form's id) while staying strict when a normal page
  loses its form.
- Suite: 892 PASS (http 120 / pos 384 / shop 118 / role 48 /
  crud_contract 175 / mysql 41 / https 6).

## Phase 25 - Child add-form 404: single-line action URLs (suite 893 PASS)
- Bug: confirming an inline child add row flashed "Request failed (HTTP
  404) - your input was kept". The <c></c> tt conversion (84b74d95)
  reflowed the child form's action attribute in md_child_tab.h.tt over
  several source lines, so the rendered HTML kept a newline + indent
  spaces between crud_path and /create. WHATWG URL parsing strips the
  newline but percent-encodes the spaces, so the browser POSTed to
  /pos/x%20...%20/create -> no route -> 404.
- Why the suite never caught it: tests POST to hand-built URLs; only a
  browser uses the parsed action. Fix = the action is one line again
  (plus &amp; for the redirect), exactly like the master forms.
- Sweep: a scan of every action=/href=/formaction=/src= value in
  display/**.tt for embedded newlines found this as the only offender.
- Tests: new pin on /pos/roles - any form action carrying whitespace
  fails (currently []). The 3 tab-strip pins (Live active, ?live=1,
  Trash active) went whitespace-tolerant (re.search with \s*): the same
  conversion moved the Live/Trash labels onto their own lines and HTML
  collapses that text whitespace. Rule: whitespace in an attribute URL
  is a hard error; whitespace between an attribute and its text content
  is harmless - pin accordingly.
- Also in this commit: md_child_query_row.h.tt's legacy ?q+?qcol
  ternary un-nested into an if/else (shown/shown_s), keeping the
  queryable guard open around the select/input so shown_s stays in
  scope and non-queryable columns still render an empty cell; the
  <option> start tag regained its closing > (dropped in the reformat -
  without it the label and selected were swallowed as malformed
  attributes) and the 3 dropdown pins became whitespace-tolerant for
  the same reason as the tab pins.
- Suite: 893 PASS (http 120 / pos 385 / shop 118 / role 48 /
  crud_contract 175 / mysql 41 / https 6).

## Phase 26 - Soft-delete cascade across relationships (suite 897 PASS)
- Soft-delete is now a RELATIONSHIP property, not per-table: a trigger
  pair per edge stamps children.deleted_at when the parent is deleted
  and clears it on restore (0003 s9, 25 triggers). New: categories
  (recursive), languages, customers, roles, staff->cash,
  inventory_stocks->stock_ledger.
- Self-referencing hierarchies (org_units.parent_id,
  categories.parent_id) needed WITH RECURSIVE bodies: a plain AFTER
  UPDATE trigger only touches the rows the statement hit, so deleting a
  root stamped its children and STOPPED - grandchildren kept rendering
  under a deleted root. Both walk the whole subtree now. Verified over
  real HTTP: POST /pos/categories/L1/delete stamped L1, L2, L3 and a
  product under L3 with the same timestamp; restore cleared all four.
- Stamping alone still lets a live row reference a deleted parent, so
  md_fk_options_where() adds deleted_at IS NULL (ANDed with the column's
  fk_where, never replacing it) to the FK dropdown and the header
  filter. md_fk_display() deliberately does NOT gate - it falls back to
  its own ungated label query so such a row renders its name, not a
  raw uuid.
- The gate is shared by create AND update: on the update form it made a
  row with a deleted parent render no `selected`, so a plain submit
  silently re-pointed the FK at the first listed parent. Fix =
  md_opt_has_id() + one extra `<option selected>` in the master edit
  row, emitted only when the row's own value is missing from the live
  list. Picking stays gated; editing never rewrites what you had. The
  child-row update form is an empty JS-driven stub and needed nothing.
- users->notes intentionally has NO cascade: notes (0001) has no
  deleted_at column. Documented in 0003 s9 rather than back-filled into
  a frozen migration.
- 0007 must track 0003: it renames `users`, so its header contract is
  "drop every object naming users in its body before the RENAME". The
  customer cascade triggers name users, so they joined the drop list and
  are recreated verbatim. 0007 also carries VERBATIM copies of the
  org_units triggers - refreshed to the recursive bodies, or 0007 would
  silently overwrite the 0003 fix on every rebuild.
- cash_shifts -> cash: clean rename, no ALTER migration (base files
  edited in place, history rewritten, golden regenerated). data-tab
  derives from children[].table, so the tab/table-list pins moved too.
- 0011_seed_config (all 3 dialects, registered in db.c) seeds
  pos.shop_name: /pos/config is never empty on a fresh DB. The test
  pins the CONTRACT - live row, non-empty, not encrypted, storefront
  renders that exact string - not a literal, because the seed value is
  a product decision.
- Harness fixes these changes exposed: `selected` (like `required`) is
  a bare attribute ATTR_RE cannot see -> has_attr() scans the raw attr
  string, word-bounded; required selects now skip options a live row
  already holds (a UNIQUE FK earned a 409 and the create leg never got
  its row); shop_test's selected pin went whitespace-tolerant to match
  pos_test.
- Suite: 897 PASS (http 120 / pos 389 / shop 118 / role 48 /
  crud_contract 175 / mysql 41 / https 6).

## Phase 27 - Geo hierarchy + cascading village picker (suite 908 PASS)

**Schema.** The four admin tables (provinces / districts / communes /
villages) now live in **0003 section 2, before users and staff** - they were
in 0009, which 0003 referenced forward. 0009_geo_admin is now **seed only**.
`locations` is gone from every dialect, from 0004/0007, from the goldens and
from the tests; `staff.village_id` / `users.village_id` point at
`villages(id)` instead.

`id` is the surrogate PK and the official MOC code rides along as `prov_id` /
`dist_id` / `comm_id` / `vill_id`, deliberately **not** as the key: the source
export ships a renumbered duplicate district (Odongkmeachey, codes 505 and
509, same province), commune codes are unique only within a district, and
village codes only within a commune (160 byte-identical duplicate rows were
deduped). FKs target `id`.

**Picker (requirement: province -> district -> commune -> village, fast).**
`js/GeoCascade.js` drives it:

- Ancestors are embedded ONCE per page as inert JSON in
  `<script type="application/json" data-geo-data>` shaped
  `{"p":[[id,parent,name]],"d":[...],"c":[...],"s":{village_id:commune_id}}`
  - 44 + 227 + 1712 rows, ~130 KB. Filtering is pure array work, zero
    round-trips; rows are indexed by parent in a Map.
- Villages (14,858 rows, ~2.1 MB as options) are **never** embedded. They
  are fetched per chosen commune from `GET /geo/villages?commune=<id>`
  (bound params) which answers bare `<option>` lines, cached per commune.
- `"s"` maps only the villages already chosen on THIS page, so an edit form
  can walk a stored village back up to its province without shipping 14,858
  rows.
- The three ancestor selects carry **no `name`** - they are UI-only
  navigation, so the form still posts exactly one field, `village_id`.
- Re-armed on `md:swapped` (dispatched from `mdSwap()`), because that
  replaces `#mc-root` wholesale.

Cascade columns skip the bulk option loaders (`md_form_cols_load`,
`md_col_load_options`) - `md_fk_display` falls back to a one-row lookup,
cheaper than 14,858 rows.

**The village filter is a text box, not a dropdown.** `md_child_query_row`
falls through to the `<input>` for `fk_cascade` columns: its option list is
~1.7 MB, and the search builder already matches an FK column against its
live parent's **label** through `EXISTS (... AND mdq.name_kh LIKE '%x%')`, so
typing part of a Khmer village name narrows the list for free.

**`?nojs=1` - the one place output varies.** `wiki` hard rule 67 says the
server is byte-identical with JS disabled. The cascade makes the village leaf
JS-dependent (server ships only `None`), so a scripting-off browser could
never satisfy `staff.village_id NOT NULL`. Each cascade page therefore emits
a tiny `<noscript><meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=...&nojs=1">`
that preserves the rest of the query. On that render `geo_data` is NULL, so
the refresh is not re-emitted (exactly one hop, no loop) and the CREATE form
ships the full list. The list is deliberately **not** given to the inline
update forms: their `master-edit-btn` is a `type="button"` toggled by
ListExpandSwitcher.js, so with scripting off those rows never open and the
copy would be ~2 MB per row of dead weight. Sizes: 247 KB with JS,
2.5 MB on `?nojs=1`.

**Two real bugs this work found:**
1. **MySQL naive `;` split.** `driver_mysql.c:3-4` documents the contract -
   "no semicolons inside comments or strings" - and a `(UUID default);`
   inside a 0003 header comment made `sql_exec_script` error. SQLite uses a
   real parser and is unaffected; postgres is a wire stub (fixed anyway).
2. **`String_Builder` is not NUL-terminated** (nob.h:679).
   `md_cascade_json` did `temp_strdup(sb.items)` without `sb_append_null`,
   so it read past `sb.count` into heap still holding the migration script -
   injecting raw `INSERT INTO villages...` bytes (cut mid-UTF-8) into
   `/pos/users` and failing `body.decode()` in two suites. Every other
   `temp_strdup(sb.items)` site in the repo already appends the NUL.

- Tests: `db_fk_target()`/`db_cascade_value()` let the contract scraper pick
  a real village for a required cascade leaf (it cannot run the JS that would
  have filled it); +10 checks pinning the lazy leaf, the `?nojs=1` hop and the
  text filter. Suite: 908 PASS (http 120 / pos 389 / shop 118 / role 48 /
  crud_contract 186 / mysql 41 / https 6).

## Gotchas
- String_View: use designated initializers { .data=..., .count=... }.
- String_View with data=NULL binds SQL NULL (not '') - initialize
  form-derived views with sv_from_cstr("") before `= ''` tautologies.
- No sb_append_ch — use sb_append_buf(sb, &c, 1).
- tt-generated headers are hex — grep for hex escapes, not literal text.
- Demo tests assume default per_page=20 shows everything (row counts < 20) —
  keep demo seeds small; POS volume seeds live in POS migration/test only.
- Old notes have user_id NULL -> invisible under any master in /people.
- Never delete resource/image/upload/7155395830974148_1.webp.
- User had uncommitted deletions (core/display/table.c/h + display/table.h.tt)
  + route.c edits as of 2026-10-04 — verify build/tests BEFORE new work.
- **MySQL/Postgres drivers split scripts naively on `;`** — never put a
  semicolon inside a comment or string in those dialects (SQLite uses a real
  parser and tolerates them). `driver_mysql.c:3-4` states the contract.
- **`String_Builder` is NOT NUL-terminated** (nob.h:679). Any
  `temp_strdup(sb.items)` needs `sb_append_null(&sb)` first, or it reads past
  `sb.count` into whatever heap follows.

# Simplexity

The project rule. Not "keep it simple" as an excuse to skip the work —
**the work is genuinely complex, so the code must not add more.**

A server-side web framework has irreducible complexity:

- Parsing HTTP without leaking or hanging on a hostile client.
- Keeping HTML, SQL and C in sync across three database dialects.
- Rendering pages fast enough that the approach is worth choosing over a
  framework someone else already wrote.
- Allowing a new resource to be added without editing the router, the render
  engine and the schema layer in lockstep.

None of that can be wished away. Simplexity says: **solve exactly that much,
and stop.** Every line that is not solving one of those problems is a line that
makes the real problems harder to see.

## The rules

1. **Plain C, no cleverness.** A `switch` beats a table of function pointers
   until you have 20 cases. Linear code that reads top-to-bottom beats a state
   machine that needs a diagram. A struct with 6 fields beats a struct with 6
   fields and an inheritance shim.

2. **No framework a human did not write.** webc vendors three single-file
   libraries — `nob` (build), the SQLite amalgamation, and a coroutine
   scheduler — and calls two system libraries, OpenSSL and libmariadb, both
   **optional**: the build gateway drops each one (and the feature behind it)
   when the host lacks it instead of failing the build. It does
   not build a router DSL, an ORM, a dependency injector, or a plugin system
   ahead of needing one. The router is an array of 20 structs.

3. **Compile the HTML, do not interpret it.** Templates are turned into C by
   `tt` at build time and compiled with the program. There is no template
   engine in the binary, no string scanning per request, and no second
   language to learn at runtime. See [templates.md](templates.md).

4. **Errors are values.** Fallible functions return `bool`. Failure paths use
   `return_defer` into a single `defer:` label rather than nested cleanup.
   There is no `longjmp` and no hidden global error state. Where a message
   needs human context, it is printed at the point of failure with file and
   line (`LOG_SQLITE3_ERROR`).

5. **Generated is generated.** `build/` and `build/h_to_html/` are outputs.
   Nothing in them is ever hand-edited, and nothing in them is checked in as a
   source of truth. If a generated file needs a change, change the input.

6. **No speculative abstraction — and when one slips in, say so.** Two similar
   things are two things; the third time, consider factoring. `src/crud/`
   currently violates this (a declarative CRUD API with no callers), and it is
   recorded as a gap rather than quietly left in place. Honesty about a
   violation costs a paragraph; pretending it is architecture costs the next
   reader an hour.

7. **The caller owns the memory, and the docs say who frees what.** Any
   function that returns a pointer or a `String_Builder` documents the owner.
   `crud_rows_free`, `crud_form_options_free`, `MD_ChildRows` and the pool's
   `db_close` release path all exist because ownership is stated rather than
   inferred.

8. **Test the parsing before the pretty part.** Route parsing, form extraction,
   migration history and the HTTP body cap get tests before a page is styled.
   The suites run against a throwaway `$HOME` so no test can damage a real
   database — see [testing.md](testing.md).

9. **Prefer fewer, larger files over many tiny ones.** File count is not
   modularity. `serve.c` at ~620 lines doing I/O, TLS, parsing and response
   rendering is simpler than four files that share connection state by
   convention.

10. **If a page in this wiki is needed to understand a function, the function
    is too clever.** Rename or restructure until it reads on its own.

## What Simplexity explicitly allows

- Long functions when they are linear and read top-to-bottom.
- Duplicating a small amount of logic to avoid a bad abstraction.
- Shipping a feature for one dialect before the others, **as long as the
  limitation is logged** — which is exactly how Postgres is handled: the
  dialect is first-class in schema and queries, the driver is an honest stub
  that fails with a clear message instead of a silent wrong answer.
- Leaving a known wart visible in [dev-log.md](dev-log.md) rather than
  restructuring to hide it.

## What it forbids

- A "core framework" written before the second subsystem needs it.
- Macro magic beyond the handful in `webc_template.h` and `nob.h` that earn
  their keep — and those two files are the entire sanctioned surface.
- Cleverness that needs a comment to explain the control flow.
- A TODO with no corresponding entry in the dev log.
- Two ways to do the same thing (there must not be a hand-written CRUD path
  *and* a macro-generated one both in service; today there is — see
  [dev-log.md](dev-log.md)).

# webc wiki

This directory is the project's **memory**. It lives in the repo on purpose: the
history of *why the code is the way it is* is as much a deliverable as the code.

If you are an agent or a human picking this up cold, read in this order:

1. [simplexity.md](simplexity.md) — the rules we build under. Read before writing anything.
2. [architecture.md](architecture.md) — how a request becomes bytes, and where each piece lives.
3. [dev-log.md](dev-log.md) — what is done, what is next, what broke, what is knowingly wrong.
4. [decisions.md](decisions.md) — one entry per architectural choice, with the
   rejected alternatives. Check here before inventing a new pattern.

## Map

| Page | What it answers |
|---|---|
| [simplexity.md](simplexity.md) | What rules constrain the code we write? |
| [architecture.md](architecture.md) | How does a request flow, and what is in which file? |
| [templates.md](templates.md) | How does HTML become a C function? |
| [database.md](database.md) | How do three SQL dialects share one schema? |
| [testing.md](testing.md) | How do we run the app without touching a real database? |
| [cli.md](cli.md) | What is the command-line contract for users and agents? |
| [decisions.md](decisions.md) | Why did we do it this way and not that way? |
| [dev-log.md](dev-log.md) | Where are we right now? |
| [other_wiki_put_here.md](other_wiki_put_here.md) | Placeholder — no page has claimed it yet. |

## How to keep this wiki honest

- **A decision is not a decision until it is written down here.** If you changed
  something and did not update the wiki, the change is not finished.
- **The dev log is append-mostly.** Add a dated section at the top. Do not rewrite
  old entries; if something turned out wrong, say so in the new entry.
- **Status means "compiles and is covered by a test",** not "the file exists".
- **Write down what is broken too.** A wiki that only records successes teaches
  the next reader to trust code that should not be trusted. The known gaps in
  [dev-log.md](dev-log.md) are load-bearing.
- Keep pages short. If a page is long, it is really two pages.

## Conventions used across these pages

- **`display/*.tt`** are hand-written. **`build/h_to_html/**.h`** are generated
  from them and are never edited.
- **`src/crud/`** and the **postgres driver** are in-tree but not wired to
  anything that runs. Both are described as such wherever they appear — see
  [dev-log.md](dev-log.md).
- Line counts and file references were measured on 2026-10-15, not guessed.

# Database

How three SQL dialects share one schema, one pool and one migration history.

## Choosing a dialect and a database

Environment resolution happens once in `main()` (`src/webc.c`) before
anything touches the database. Four variables plus one compiled-in constant,
no config file:

| Variable | Role | Precedence |
|---|---|---|
| `WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL` | pin the dialect: `SQLITE3` / `MYSQL` / `POSTGRES` (case-insensitive). Overrides prefix detection | wins over the prefix, dialect only |
| `WEBC_DB` | full DSN or file path (tests, alternate instances) | wins for the location |
| `WEBC_CONNECTION_STRING` | raw DSN, read only when `WEBC_DB` is unset | fallback |
| `WEBC_DEFAULT_DSN` | **compiled-in** constant above `main()` in `src/webc.c` — edit it and rebuild to point the binary somewhere else permanently (e.g. the `mysql:` DSN) | fallback to env |
| *(none)* | nothing — **no connection is ever attempted**, DB routes answer "no database configured" | no default |

`webc_db_lang()` (`src/db/db.c:599`) picks the dialect in three steps:

1. `WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL` is set → that dialect (an unknown value logs an error
   and falls through to step 2).
2. `mysql:` / `postgres:` prefix on `WEBC_DB_PATH`.
3. Anything else (including `WEBC_DB_PATH == NULL`) → SQLite.

`webc_db_dsn()` then hands the driver the string with the prefix stripped, so
the driver never sees the selector.

| `WEBC_DB` | Dialect | Driver |
|---|---|---|
| unset, `WEBC_DEFAULT_DSN` also empty | — | no connection attempted |
| unset, `WEBC_DEFAULT_DSN` set (e.g. `~/sqlite3/webc_c/db`) | SQLite | bundled amalgamation (3.46.1); leading `~/` expands to `$HOME` |
| `/tmp/x.db` | SQLite | bundled amalgamation |
| `mysql:user=root;password=;database=webc;socket=/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock` | MySQL/MariaDB | libmariadb |
| `postgres:...` | PostgreSQL | **stub — fails with a clear message** |
| `WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL=MYSQL` + any path | MySQL/MariaDB | pin wins over the path |

For a SQLite file DSN the parent directory becomes `WEBC_DIR_PATH`, which is
where the runtime creates what it needs (including the recursive
`nested/deep/db` the test harness deliberately exercises). A
`mysql:`/`postgres:` DSN is not a file path, so `WEBC_DIR_PATH` becomes `.`
and the legacy file→directory layout dance is skipped (it only runs for the
SQLite dialect anyway).

### More than one database per process

`webc_open_db_spec(spec)` (`src/db/db.h`) opens an **additional** database —
`"mysql:..."`, `"postgres:..."` or a SQLite path — independent of the primary
global. An explicit prefix on `spec` wins even when `WEBC_DEFAULT_SQL` pins
the primary; a prefix-less `spec` honours the pin. Not pooled: the caller owns
the handle and must `db_close()` it. Schema verification is cached per
`(dialect, DSN)` pair, so opening the same second database twice does not
re-read the migration history.

**The design is one server per process.** This API is opt-in and no
production code calls it — nothing in `webc` opens a second SQL server by
design; every pool slot opens the same primary DSN.

### Why SQLite is the default dialect

It needs no server, no credentials and no daemon, so a clone builds and runs
against a file with no server setup. Everything else is opt-in through one
variable — and if nothing is configured at all, no connection is attempted
rather than guessing a path.

### Postgres: honest stub

`src/db/driver_postgres.c` is a complete `Sql_Driver` vtable in which every
function fails:

```c
static bool pg_drv_open(db_t *db, const char *dsn) {
    (void) dsn;
    if (db) snprintf(db->err, sizeof(db->err), "postgres driver is not implemented yet");
    return false;
}
```

The dialect is **first-class everywhere else** — `q[]` query tables have a
`[SQL_POSTGRES]` entry, `migrations_table_sql[SQL_POSTGRES]` exists, every
migration directory has a `postgres.sql`. Only the wire protocol is missing.

This is deliberate, and the alternative was worse: dropping Postgres from the
schema layer would mean rewriting the whole query table when it is implemented,
and pretending it connects would fail somewhere obscure. Failing in
`db_open()` with a sentence naming the problem is the cheapest possible
mistake. See [decisions.md](decisions.md) D4.

## The driver interface — `src/db/sql.h`

One vtable, four functions, plus column access:

```c
open / close / prepare / step / finalize / column_text
```

`sql.h` gives callers a dialect-neutral statement API — `db_t`, `sql_stmt`,
`sql_step()` returning `SQL_ROW`/`SQL_DONE`/`SQL_ERROR` — so feature code never
branches on dialect for reads. Dialect differences are confined to:

- `driver_*.c`
- `migrations_table_sql[]`
- `migrations/<name>/{sqlite3,mysql,postgres}.sql`
- the `[SQL_*]` entries in per-file query tables

| Driver | Lines | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `driver_sqlite.c` | 172 | bundled, `third_party/sqlite-amalgamation-3460100` |
| `driver_mysql.c` | 481 | libmariadb, found via `pkg-config` at build time; **optional** - built as a stub when the host lacks libmariadb (see the feature gateway in [architecture.md](architecture.md)) |
| `driver_postgres.c` | 101 | stub |

### MySQL porting idioms

- `mysql_drv_open()` sets `sql_mode PIPES_AS_CONCAT` once per connection, so
  `a || b` concatenates like in the SQLite dialect (verified: no
  mysql-dialect SQL uses `||` as logical OR). Seed files stay line-for-line
  ports: `INSERT IGNORE`, `DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL n DAY)` for
  `strftime`, `LPAD` for `printf`, and comma-joins where MySQL's JOIN
  precedence would reject `FROM a, b JOIN c ON ... a.x` (the `ON` cannot see
  `a`).
- The naive `;` splitter in `driver_mysql.c` has one contract: **no `;`
  inside comments or string literals** — a `;` in a comment splits the
  statement in half.
- The dialect is **optional at build time**: `nob.c`'s feature gateway
  compiles `driver_mysql.c` as a stub when the host has no libmariadb, and a
  `mysql:` DSN then fails at `db_open()` with "mysql support not compiled
  in" (the same shape as the postgres stub). Nothing else in webc changes.
- `0004_seed_pos/mysql.sql` carries the real seed data: missing test coverage
  must not strip data from a dialect. Its Postgres twin stays comment-only
  (stub driver).

## The pool

```c
#define DB_POOL_SIZE 8          // src/db/db.h
db_t *open_webc_db(void);       // checkout from the pool (or a transient)
void  db_close(db_t *db);       // pooled -> release, otherwise destroy
```

The pool is **lazy**: nothing connects at startup (`serve.c` does not warm
it), so serving static files or a refused DSN never costs a connection. The
first checkout opens connection 1; later checkouts grow toward
`DB_POOL_SIZE` only while every slot is genuinely busy.

`db_pool_get()` is a real **checkout**: it scans for the next slot whose
`in_use` flag is clear, marks it taken, and `db_close()` hands it back
(`db_pool_release()` rolls back any open transaction and recycles a SQLite
connection that leaked prepared statements). Handlers keep the unchanged
`db = open_webc_db(); ...; db_close(db);` shape — the pool is invisible to
them.

Two safety valves:

- **Pool exhausted** (all slots checked out): `db_pool_get()` grows the pool
  if it can, and otherwise opens a transient connection instead of returning
  `NULL`, so concurrency costs a connection, not a 500. A failed *grow* never
  latches — only the first-ever open does.
- **First open failure latches**: a bad DSN or a refused schema marks the pool
  dead for the process. `db_pool_get()` then returns `NULL` immediately with
  one log line — no per-request retry storm re-running the 2.4 MB history
  check. Callers already treat `NULL` as "serve 500".

Schema verification itself runs **once per process per `(dialect, DSN)`**
(`verified_items` in `db.c`); every later open of the same database just gets
a fresh connection.

## Migrations

### Layout

```
migrations/
  0001_notes/
    sqlite3.sql    mysql.sql    postgres.sql
  0002_users/
    sqlite3.sql    mysql.sql    postgres.sql
```

Numbered directory = migration name; three dialect files inside. Registered
in a **compile-time array** in `db.c`, not discovered at runtime:

```c
static const Migration migrations[] = {
    { "0001_notes", { [SQL_SQLITE] = "migrations/0001_notes/sqlite3.sql",
                      [SQL_MYSQL]  = "migrations/0001_notes/mysql.sql",
                      [SQL_POSTGRES] = "..." } },
    { "0002_users", { ... } },
};
```

A migration that exists on disk but is not in `migrations[]` **does not run**.
Adding a migration means adding the directory *and* an array entry.

### The history table

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Migrations (
    applied_at DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    query      TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

(`TIMESTAMP` instead of `DATETIME` on Postgres; `query LONGTEXT` on MySQL —
this is why the DDL is a per-dialect array rather than one string. Databases
created when MySQL still said `TEXT` (64 KiB cap) are widened in place with a
best-effort `ALTER TABLE Migrations MODIFY query LONGTEXT NOT NULL;` on every
open — a migration file larger than 64 KiB would otherwise fail to store.)

`query` stores the **exact text of the migration that was applied**, not a
version number. On every open the code compares stored strings against the
current files.

Why not a version number: it cannot detect that an already-applied migration
was edited. Storing the text turns "someone rewrote history" from silent data
corruption into a detectable state.

The compare is **order-independent**: the `Migrations` table has no key and no
`ORDER BY` can be relied on (MySQL's hidden PK, Postgres row order), so every
stored row must equal some `migrations[]` entry and vice versa — the counts
bound it. A row that matches nothing is `SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH`.

### The open sequence

`create_schema_status()`:

```
schema verified already for (lang, DSN)?  -- yes: skip straight to a fresh conn
migration_files_load(lang)     -- read the three files, cache per dialect
sql_txn_begin()
exec migrations_table_sql[]    -- ensure Migrations exists (+ LONGTEXT widen)
SELECT query FROM Migrations
compare stored vs current files, order-independent
  more in DB than in code   → ERROR "Database scheme is too new..."
  a stored string differs   → SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH
  pending                   → apply them all now
sql_txn_commit()
```

**Everything runs in one transaction.** Two consequences, both encoded as
comments in `db.c`:

1. Migration files must not contain `PRAGMA` statements — SQLite rejects
   `journal_mode`/`synchronous` changes inside a transaction. Connection
   PRAGMAs (`cache_size`, `temp_store`, `mmap_size`, `foreign_keys`, ...)
   run in `sqlite_drv_open()` — at open time, before any transaction.
2. A failure commits nothing; there is no partially-migrated state.

Set `WEBC_TRACE_MIGRATION_QUERIES=1` to print each migration's SQL as it
applies.

### When history mismatches: rebuild, keep the data

```c
if (status == SCHEMA_HISTORY_MISMATCH && attempt == 0) {
    db_backup_and_reset(dsn);       // dsn = this connection's own DSN,
                                    // db → db.bak (+ wal/shm), close first
    // fresh db created and migrated from migrations[]
    db_restore_from_backup(...)     // copy shared tables/columns
}
```

The recipe, verbatim from the comment at `db.c:349`:

1. `db` → `db.bak` (old file, untouched)
2. fresh db is created and migrated from `migrations[]`
3. every table/column **both** databases share is copied from `db.bak` into the
   new schema

What it tolerates, each logged as `INFO:`:

- backup table with no counterpart → skipped
- table sharing no columns → skipped
- more than `MAX_TABLE_COLS` columns, or more tables than the array holds →
  refused with an explicit error rather than a partial copy

What it does **not** cover:

- **SQLite only.** `db_restore_from_backup()` takes a `sqlite3*`, so a
  history mismatch on MySQL/MariaDB is not auto-repaired.
- `db.bak` is overwritten on the next mismatch — keep a copy if it matters.

### Migration ordering note

`0001_notes` deliberately has **no `REFERENCES` clause** on `notes.user_id`:
the `users` table does not exist until `0002_users`. The comment in the file
says so. Cross-table integrity between the two is therefore not enforced by
the schema.

### IDs

```sql
id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (UUID())          -- sqlite/mysql
id TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT (gen_random_uuid()::text) -- postgres
```

IDs are **text**, not integers. `parse_uri_id()` in `route.c` tags an
all-digits segment as `ID_INT` so a legacy integer-keyed table still routes;
everything else flows through as text. See [architecture.md](architecture.md).

### Golden files

`test/golden/` pins the `sqlite3.sql` files **byte for byte**. Existing
databases hold those exact strings in `Migrations.query`, so editing a
`sqlite3.sql` that has already shipped is a history mismatch for every user of
that database — which is precisely why the golden test exists. See
[testing.md](testing.md).

The rule when a shipped migration *must* be edited: amend the golden to the
new bytes **in the same commit** — the alternative (moving the change into a
new numbered migration) is only correct when no deployed database carries the
old bytes. `0003_pos_eshop` was amended this way on 2026-11-05: the
`v_geo_hierarchy` view added by `ff4fc0ed` already sits in the live database's
history, so a new `0012` migration would have forced a D5 rebuild of every
existing database instead of a golden re-pin.

## Things that will bite you

| | |
|---|---|
| Editing a shipped migration file (without re-pinning the golden) | history mismatch on every existing SQLite DB |
| Adding a file without a `migrations[]` entry | silently never applied |
| `PRAGMA` inside a migration file | fails — it runs inside a transaction |
| `WEBC_DB` with only a `mysql:` prefix change | no directory is derived (`WEBC_DIR_PATH` = `.`); only the DSN moves |
| Pool failure | latched for the process — one log line, then `NULL` → 500, no retry storm |
| Postgres | `db_open()` fails with "postgres driver is not implemented yet" |
